items.title: Desktop polls ~89 req/min at idle — inventory + move the always-on surfaces to events
items.body:
## Summary

Desktop drives its live surfaces with timers rather than events. With the app open, the
gateway connected, one chat focused, no pet, and the user doing nothing, the renderer
fires roughly **89 network/IPC round-trips per minute from 7 always-on timers**. Two of
them account for 60 of the 89. Mount a few more panes and it clears 150/min.

Nothing is broken — this is a latency and idle-cost issue. Every polled surface is stale
by up to its interval, and the wakeups cost battery for work that has a precise trigger
already sitting in the gateway.

This is the desktop-side inventory. The cross-process half of the problem is #58671
(externally-driven turns never reach clients as events, so every consumer writes its own
poller); several rows below are that issue's symptom in this app.

Audit taken against `e45f2b39e`.

## Tier A — always-on polls

Running whenever the app is open. This is the list worth killing.

| What | File | Cadence | req/min | Event source today? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `session.active_list` — sidebar liveness/stall/reap | [`use-background-sync.ts#L263`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/e45f2b39e/apps/desktop/src/app/contrib/hooks/use-background-sync.ts#L263) | 1.5s | **40** | no `session.state_changed` broadcast |
| `pet.info` / `pet.info.meta` | [`floating-pet.tsx#L205`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/e45f2b39e/apps/desktop/src/components/pet/floating-pet.tsx#L205) | 3s idle / 15s active | **20** | none — `/pet` writes config, emits nothing |
| plugin dir rescan (readdir IPC) | [`runtime-loader.ts#L331`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/e45f2b39e/apps/desktop/src/contrib/runtime-loader.ts#L331) | 5s | **12** | partial — plugin *files* are fs-watched, the *directory* is not |
| `messaging.sessions` list | [`use-background-sync.ts#L290`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/e45f2b39e/apps/desktop/src/app/contrib/hooks/use-background-sync.ts#L290) | 10s | **6** | none (#58671) |
| `getStatus()` + runtime readiness (2 legs) | [`use-status-snapshot.ts#L28`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/e45f2b39e/apps/desktop/src/app/shell/hooks/use-status-snapshot.ts#L28) | 15s | **8** | none |
| cron job list | [`use-background-sync.ts#L280`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/e45f2b39e/apps/desktop/src/app/contrib/hooks/use-background-sync.ts#L280) | 30s | **2** | none — scheduler ticks in-process, emits nothing |
| pool keepalive | [`use-gateway-boot.ts#L417`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/e45f2b39e/apps/desktop/src/app/gateway/hooks/use-gateway-boot.ts#L417) | 60s | 1 | correct as-is — a heartbeat, not a poll |
| update check | [`updates.ts#L681`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/e45f2b39e/apps/desktop/src/store/updates.ts#L681) | 30min | ~0 | fine |

The pet poll is inverted: `active` is false when you *don't have a pet*, so users with no
pet poll hardest — 20 req/min, forever, for a cosmetic feature whose only trigger is
someone typing `/pet`.

## Tier B — mount-scoped polls

Only while that surface is open, so cheaper, but each one tails something the backend
already knows changed.

| What | File | Cadence |
|---|---|---|
| MCP log tail | [`mcp-tab.tsx#L1559`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/e45f2b39e/apps/desktop/src/app/skills/mcp-tab.tsx#L1559) | 2s |
| gateway log tail | [`gateway-menu-panel.tsx#L62`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/e45f2b39e/apps/desktop/src/app/shell/gateway-menu-panel.tsx#L62) | 3s |
| file-tree fallback re-probe (error state only) | [`use-project-tree.ts#L468`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/e45f2b39e/apps/desktop/src/app/right-sidebar/files/use-project-tree.ts#L468) | 3s |
| contrib `LogsPane` (`refetchInterval`) | [`panes.tsx#L42`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/e45f2b39e/apps/desktop/src/app/contrib/panes.tsx#L42) | 5s |
| background processes (while one runs) | [`status-stack/index.tsx#L121`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/e45f2b39e/apps/desktop/src/app/chat/composer/status-stack/index.tsx#L121) | 5s |
| active messaging transcript | [`use-background-sync.ts#L301`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/e45f2b39e/apps/desktop/src/app/contrib/hooks/use-background-sync.ts#L301) | 5s |
| messaging platform status | [`messaging/index.tsx#L157`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/e45f2b39e/apps/desktop/src/app/messaging/index.tsx#L157) | 6s |
| cron runs — page | [`cron/index.tsx#L709`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/e45f2b39e/apps/desktop/src/app/cron/index.tsx#L709) | 8s |
| cron runs — sidebar peek | [`cron-jobs-section.tsx#L345`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/e45f2b39e/apps/desktop/src/app/chat/sidebar/cron-jobs-section.tsx#L345) | 8s |
| billing state | [`use-billing-state.ts#L25`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/e45f2b39e/apps/desktop/src/app/settings/billing/use-billing-state.ts#L25) | 30s |

Most of Tier A and B already gate on `document.visibilityState` through `visiblePoll()`,
so the cost lands while the user is looking at the surface — which is also exactly when
the staleness shows.

## Tier C — bounded handshakes, leave alone

These wait on a one-shot operation with a defined end. Converting them to events buys
nothing: `hub-actions.ts#L95`, `system-actions.ts#L21`, `maintenance.tsx#L102`,
`onboarding.ts#L603` (OAuth device code), `updates.ts#L474`,
`use-prompt-actions/utils.ts#L117`.

## Tier D — clock ticks, out of scope

About 12 timers that only `setState` to repaint elapsed time — no I/O, and no event to
subscribe to. Worth a separate look for re-render pressure, not for this issue: notably
[`agents/index.tsx#L197`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/e45f2b39e/apps/desktop/src/app/agents/index.tsx#L197)
(500ms while any agent runs) and
[`chat-swap-overlay.tsx#L28`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/e45f2b39e/apps/desktop/src/app/chat/chat-swap-overlay.tsx#L28)
(80ms). [`glyph-spinner.tsx#L48`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/e45f2b39e/apps/desktop/src/components/ui/glyph-spinner.tsx#L48)
already has the right instinct and gates itself.

## Electron main

`electron/backend-ready.ts#L172` stats a ready-file every **50ms** during cold start —
bounded, but `fs.watch` on the dir would do it. The OAuth cookie loops
(`main.ts#L5874`, `#L6392`, 750ms) already sit behind three real `did-navigate*` events as
a fallback and are correct. The pool idle reaper (`main.ts#L7889`, 60s, self-clearing) and
the remote-lifecycle ready waits (750s, bounded) are fine.

## What actually blocks this

The gateway has exactly one global broadcast mechanism and one event flowing through it.
[`_broadcast_global_event`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/e45f2b39e/tui_gateway/server.py#L1376)
has two callers, both `skin.changed`. Everything else goes through `_emit`, scoped to a
session id and riding that session's transport.

So the top three Tier A rows are not lazy renderer code — there is nothing to subscribe to:

- **cron** — `InProcessCronScheduler`
  ([`cron/scheduler_provider.py#L162`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/e45f2b39e/cron/scheduler_provider.py#L162))
  runs a 60s daemon thread inside `gateway/run.py`. It knows the instant a job fires and
  tells nobody.
- **messaging** — inbound turns are handled in `gateway/run.py` and written to the DB; the
  desktop socket never hears about it. This is #58671.
- **live session status** — busy/idle *is* event-driven on the happy path
  (`message.start` / `message.complete`). The 1.5s poll is a deliberate backstop for turns
  that end while the socket is degraded, which the stream by definition cannot replay
  (see the comment at `use-background-sync.ts#L20-L26` and the reap block at `#L100-L135`).
  It should get cheaper, not disappear.

The template for the fix already exists in this app and works well:
[`store/workspace-events.ts`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/e45f2b39e/apps/desktop/src/store/workspace-events.ts).
Tool completion calls `notifyWorkspaceChanged()`, a throttled tick fires, and the file tree
does a surgical subtree re-read while the coding rail and review pane refresh. Its header
comment calls itself "the smart replacement for polling." That is the shape the rest of
these should take.

## Proposed direction

1. **Fan out three signals the gateway already knows** through one shared emit path:
   cron job fired/changed, messaging session updated, session state changed. This clears
   Tier A rows 1, 4 and 6 plus most of Tier B's cron rows, and is the largest single win.
   Per the root rubric this is new broadcast surface, not a new tool — but it wants one
   shared path, not three ad-hoc emitters.
2. **Keep `session.active_list` as a backstop, drop it to ~30s** once (1) exists. Removing
   it outright fights the reason it was added and brings back dark spinning rows.
3. **Pet: event, or nothing.** `/pet` writes config, and that write can emit. Failing that,
   stop polling when no pet is configured — that alone removes 20 req/min for most users
   with zero behavior change. Cheapest fix here by a wide margin.
4. **Watch the plugin directory, not just the files.** `fs.watch` on
   `<hermes home>/desktop-plugins` in main, reusing the existing
   `hermes:preview-file-changed` channel. Only the "new folder appeared" case polls today.
5. **Log tails** are the honest case for leaving a poll in place — mount-scoped and
   short-lived. Worth doing only if the goal is zero timers.

Note that (1) crosses into `tui_gateway/server.py` and `gateway/run.py`, so this is not a
desktop-only change.

items.title: `_estimate_msg_budget_tokens` charges stale reasoning to the compression tail budget — 19-24% of the budget spent on blocks no adapter replays

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
### Summary `ContextCompressor._estimate_msg_budget_tokens` (`agent/context_compressor.py`) adds `_REPLAY_BUDGET_KEYS` to every message's size, and `_find_tail_cut_by_tokens` uses that total to decide how much of the transcript survives compaction. But no adapter on `upstream/main` replays thinking for more than the newest assistant turn, so on a long thinking-model session a large fraction of the tail budget is spent on content that is provably stripped before the request is sent. The tail cut therefore lands early and each compaction discards more real transcript than the configuration intends. This is the sibling of #73298 at a **different call site**. #73298 / #73306 / #72087 all address `agent/model_metadata.py` — the preflight "should I compress?" estimator, which controls *when* compaction fires. This issue is about `agent/context_compressor.py` — the tail-budget walk, which controls *how much survives*. #73306 as written does not touch it. Measured against `upstream/main` @ `89490ae373` on a real 1,025-message session (Bedrock Converse, `global.anthropic.claude-opus-5`, 1M context, `threshold: 0.8`, `target_ratio: 0.20`). ### Mechanism ```python _REPLAY_BUDGET_KEYS = ( "reasoning", "reasoning_content", "reasoning_details", "codex_reasoning_items", "codex_message_items", ) ... for key in _REPLAY_BUDGET_KEYS: tokens += _serialized_length_for_budget(msg.get(key)) // _CHARS_PER_TOKEN ``` Charged unconditionally, for every message in history. The docstring justifies it as "these are replayed on the wire" and adds *"Accounting-only: replay fields are never mutated or pruned here"* — so the compressor charges for them and is simultaneously forbidden from reclaiming them. What the adapters actually put on the wire: | adapter | replays thinking for | evidence | |---|---|---| | `anthropic_adapter.convert_messages_to_anthropic` | **newest assistant turn only** | `idx != last_assistant_idx` strips all earlier ones; third-party / Nous-portal endpoints strip every one. Locked in by `tests/agent/test_anthropic_adapter.py::test_thinking_stripped_from_non_last_assistant` | | `bedrock_adapter.convert_messages_to_converse` | **never** | rebuilds assistant turns as `[text][toolUse]`; no reasoning branch exists (also reported as defect 3 of #36261) | | `codex_responses_adapter` | `codex_reasoning_items` (legitimate) | `replay_encrypted_reasoning` path | So `reasoning`, `reasoning_content` and `reasoning_details` should be charged for **at most one message**, and on Converse for none. ### Reproduction Synthetic, transport-level — 3 assistant turns each carrying a signed thinking block: ``` ANTHROPIC wire blocks: msg1 ['text', 'tool_use'] ← thinking stripped msg3 ['text', 'tool_use'] ← thinking stripped msg5 ['thinking', 'text', 'tool_use'] ← survives signed blocks surviving: 1 of 3 BEDROCK wire: signature present False, 'reasoningContent' present False ``` Real transcript, 866 active messages, 40 of which carry reasoning: **0 of 40** signature strings and **0 of 40** thinking strings appear in either serialized payload. (The Anthropic count is 0 rather than 1 because the newest assistant message in this particular transcript carries no reasoning.) ### Impact | | current | correct | delta | |---|---|---|---| | pre-compaction budget | 468,198 | 354,563 | **−113,635 (−24.3%)** | | post-compaction budget | 245,245 | 198,591 | **−46,654 (−19.0%)** | Replaying `_find_tail_cut_by_tokens` over the same transcript (`tail_token_budget=159344`, `protect_last_n=20`): ``` current → cut idx 359, tail preserved 666 messages corrected → cut idx 290, tail preserved 735 messages ``` **69 messages of real transcript were summarized away to make room for tokens that were never sent.** That understates the general case: in this session reasoning was concentrated in 40 of 866 messages. On a synthetic 401-message history where *every* assistant turn carries a signed thinking block, the budget inflates **4.85×** (48,111 vs 9,911) and the preserved tail collapses by roughly the same factor: | `tail_token_budget` | tail preserved (current) | tail preserved (correct) | |---|---|---| | 2,000 | 26 | 122 | | 4,000 | 50 | 242 | | 6,000 | 76 | 364 | Why the number is so large — the phantom weight is mostly *not* the thinking prose: - `signature`: 85,608 chars of opaque base64 — **72% of the reasoning mass**. Base64 tokenizes near 1.5 chars/token, so `chars // 4` is wrong in both directions at once: it understates the string's true token cost *and* charges for a string that is never transmitted. - `thinking`: 32,854 chars. - `reasoning_content`: 32,854 chars, byte-identical to `thinking` in **40/40** rows — the prose is charged twice on top of the signature. Worst single message: 174 chars of `content` + 750 chars of `tool_calls` charged as **7,008 tokens** against a correct **237**. A 30× overcharge on a message whose real payload is under 1 KB. ### Why not just delete the keys The keys were added deliberately: #55572, #51800, #45485, #59804 all fixed no-op-compaction bugs caused by hidden replay blobs being invisible to the budget. That reasoning is sound and must not regress. The narrower claim here is that they should be charged **where the transport actually replays them** — the newest assistant turn — not on every historical turn where they are provably stripped. ### Reproduction A test file reproducing all of the above against `upstream/main` @ `89490ae373` is included at the end of this issue (5 passed, 1 `xfail(strict=True)` marking the assertion a fix should flip). It verifies the transport behaviour by inspecting the serialized payload rather than by reading the adapters, so the negative claim ("these fields never ship") rests on positive evidence. Caveat for anyone reproducing independently: `_find_tail_cut_by_tokens` has a second re-walk branch for when the entire transcript fits inside `soft_ceiling` (#40803). A small fixture can land in that branch, where stripping the phantom weight makes the tail *smaller* instead of larger — that comparison is measuring the fallback, not the defect. The test guards against it by asserting the stripped total still exceeds `soft_ceiling` before comparing cut indices. ### Design constraints, not a proposal Reporting this as a measurement rather than proposing a fix — the right shape depends on decisions that belong to maintainers, and there are at least two in-flight PRs whose outcome changes the answer. Constraints I ran into that are worth having on record: 1. **A provider allowlist would be wrong.** #36261 would legitimately make Bedrock Converse start replaying reasoning, at which point a "Bedrock never replays" gate silently becomes incorrect in the opposite direction. 2. **The scope is per-transport and time-varying.** Fallback routing can change `api_mode` mid-session (`chat_completion_helpers.py`), so whatever decides chargeability has to be read at estimation time rather than cached at construction. `ContextCompressor` already receives `api_mode` (`agent_init.py` passes it; it is stored and used for telemetry today), so the information is available wherever it is wanted. 3. **The replay scope is not binary.** Anthropic is `last_assistant_only`, Converse is currently `none`, Codex Responses is `all` for `codex_reasoning_items`. A boolean flag cannot express that. 4. **The `reasoning_content` duplication is arguably a separate bug.** It holds a byte-identical copy of `reasoning_details[].thinking` in 40/40 rows here. That may be worth fixing at the persistence layer independently of the budget question. 5. **#66640** appears to be establishing per-transport replay contracts for the replay path itself; if that lands, the budget could consult the same contract rather than growing its own. Whether this is fixed in the estimator, by narrowing what gets persisted, or by whatever #73306/#72087 reconciliation produces, is a maintainer call. Happy to supply more measurements from the production session if useful. ### Test file
tests/agent/test_compressor_replay_budget_repro.py — passes on upstream/main @ 89490ae373 ```python """Reproduction coverage for the compression tail-budget replay-field defect. Sibling of #73298 (preflight estimator, ``agent/model_metadata.py``) at the *other* call site: ``ContextCompressor._estimate_msg_budget_tokens`` in ``agent/context_compressor.py``, which feeds ``_find_tail_cut_by_tokens`` and therefore decides how much transcript survives a compaction. ``_estimate_msg_budget_tokens`` charges every ``_REPLAY_BUDGET_KEYS`` field on every message. The justification is that those fields are replayed on the wire — but no adapter on main replays thinking for more than the newest assistant turn: * ``anthropic_adapter.convert_messages_to_anthropic`` strips thinking from every assistant message except the last (``idx != last_assistant_idx``), and strips all of them for third-party / Nous-portal endpoints. Pinned upstream by ``test_anthropic_adapter.py::test_thinking_stripped_from_non_last_assistant``. * ``bedrock_adapter.convert_messages_to_converse`` rebuilds assistant turns as ``[text][toolUse]`` only; there is no reasoning branch at all. * ``codex_responses_adapter`` does replay ``codex_reasoning_items`` — those two keys are legitimately chargeable there. These tests assert the CURRENT (defective) behaviour so the defect is executable, and quantify the tail-cut consequence. Under a fix, the tests marked ``xfail(strict=True)`` below should start passing. """ import json import pytest from agent.anthropic_adapter import convert_messages_to_anthropic from agent.bedrock_adapter import convert_messages_to_converse from agent.context_compressor import ( ContextCompressor, _REPLAY_BUDGET_KEYS, _estimate_msg_budget_tokens, ) # A realistic opaque signature: base64, no linguistic structure, and long. # On the measured production session signatures were 72% of the reasoning mass. SIGNATURE = "c2lnbmF0dXJlLWJsb2ItQUFBQUFB" * 8 THINKING = "Deliberating about whether the knock head reached V8 parity. " * 4 def _assistant_turn(i: int) -> list: """One assistant turn carrying a signed thinking block, plus its tool result. Mirrors what the runtime persists after a thinking-model turn: the thinking text lands in BOTH ``reasoning_details[].thinking`` and ``reasoning_content`` (byte-identical in 40/40 rows of the measured session), and the signature lands in ``reasoning_details[].signature``. """ return [ { "role": "assistant", "content": f"step {i}", "reasoning_content": THINKING, "reasoning_details": [ {"type": "thinking", "thinking": THINKING, "signature": SIGNATURE} ], "tool_calls": [ { "id": f"call_{i}", "type": "function", "function": {"name": "terminal", "arguments": '{"command":"ls"}'}, } ], }, {"role": "tool", "tool_call_id": f"call_{i}", "content": "ok"}, ] def _history(n_turns: int) -> list: msgs = [{"role": "user", "content": "go"}] for i in range(n_turns): msgs += _assistant_turn(i) return msgs def _strip_replay(msg: dict) -> dict: return {k: v for k, v in msg.items() if k not in _REPLAY_BUDGET_KEYS} class TestTransportsDoNotReplayHistoricalThinking: """Positive evidence for the negative claim: inspect the serialized payload.""" def test_anthropic_keeps_only_newest_assistant_thinking(self): _, wire = convert_messages_to_anthropic( _history(3), base_url="https://api.anthropic.com", model="claude-opus-5" ) assistants = [m for m in wire if m.get("role") == "assistant"] assert len(assistants) == 3 def n_thinking(m): return sum( 1 for b in m["content"] if isinstance(b, dict) and b.get("type") in ("thinking", "redacted_thinking") ) assert [n_thinking(m) for m in assistants] == [0, 0, 1], [ [b.get("type") for b in m["content"]] for m in assistants ] # Only one signature reaches the wire, out of three in history. assert json.dumps(wire).count(SIGNATURE) == 1 def test_bedrock_converse_never_replays_thinking(self): _, wire = convert_messages_to_converse(_history(3)) blob = json.dumps(wire) assert SIGNATURE not in blob assert THINKING not in blob assert "reasoningContent" not in blob class TestBudgetChargesFieldsThatNeverShip: def test_historical_turn_charged_for_stripped_reasoning(self): """A historical assistant turn is charged for a signature Anthropic strips.""" turn = _assistant_turn(0)[0] charged = _estimate_msg_budget_tokens(turn) bare = _estimate_msg_budget_tokens(_strip_replay(turn)) # The real payload (content + tool_calls) is under 200 chars; the # replay fields inflate the charge several-fold. assert charged > bare * 4, (charged, bare) def test_reasoning_content_duplicates_thinking_and_is_charged_twice(self): turn = _assistant_turn(0)[0] both = _estimate_msg_budget_tokens(turn) details_only = _estimate_msg_budget_tokens( {k: v for k, v in turn.items() if k != "reasoning_content"} ) # Identical prose in two keys, charged twice. assert turn["reasoning_content"] == turn["reasoning_details"][0]["thinking"] assert both > details_only @pytest.mark.xfail( strict=True, reason="defect: budget charges replay fields on turns every transport strips", ) def test_only_newest_assistant_should_be_charged_for_thinking(self): """Under a per-api_mode replay contract, historical turns cost nothing extra.""" msgs = _history(3) assistants = [m for m in msgs if m.get("role") == "assistant"] historical = assistants[:-1] for m in historical: assert _estimate_msg_budget_tokens(m) == _estimate_msg_budget_tokens( _strip_replay(m) ) @pytest.fixture() def compressor(): c = ContextCompressor.__new__(ContextCompressor) c.tail_token_budget = 4000 c.protect_last_n = 2 c.min_tail_user_messages = 1 return c class TestTailCutLosesRealMessages: def test_phantom_weight_shrinks_the_protected_tail(self, compressor): """The tail walk stops early because stripped fields consume the budget. This is the user-visible half of the defect: real transcript is summarized away to make room for tokens that are never sent. """ msgs = _history(200) stripped = [_strip_replay(m) for m in msgs] # Guard: both walks must be budget-bound, not short-circuited by the # "entire transcript fits in soft_ceiling" re-walk (#40803 path), or # the comparison below would measure that fallback instead. soft_ceiling = int(compressor.tail_token_budget * 1.5) assert sum(_estimate_msg_budget_tokens(m) for m in stripped) > soft_ceiling cut_current = compressor._find_tail_cut_by_tokens(msgs, 1) cut_correct = compressor._find_tail_cut_by_tokens(stripped, 1) tail_current = len(msgs) - cut_current tail_correct = len(msgs) - cut_correct # Measured shape: charging stripped reasoning costs ~4.8x the tail. assert tail_correct > tail_current * 4, (tail_correct, tail_current) ```

items.title: macOS: hermes update restarts only the invoking profile's launchd gateway — sibling profiles keep stale code until they crash

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: sweeper:risk-compatibility
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break existing users, config, migrations, defaults, or upgrades

items.body:
## Summary

On macOS multi-profile installs, the update's gateway-restart step is documented and implemented as fleet-wide for systemd (`hermes-gateway*` units are all restarted), but the launchd branch restarts **only the invoking profile's** LaunchAgent. Every other `ai.hermes.gateway-<profile>` service keeps running with pre-update modules cached in `sys.modules`, and fails on its **next real agent turn** — after `hermes update` printed a success message.

This is the same gap PR #41403 addressed in June; that PR is now unmergeable (dirty against main) and its author appears inactive, and the automated review's domain-resolution feedback was never addressed. Meanwhile the fleet-restart framework that landed in `_cmd_update_impl` (per-unit drain, verification, `_warn_incomplete_gateway_fleet_restart`) made the inconsistency sharper: the block's own comment says "Auto-restart ALL gateways after update", and on macOS it doesn't.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent, current `main` (also reproduced on v0.16.0 and v0.19.x)
- macOS (Apple Silicon, Darwin 24.x and 25.x) — two machines, 9–11 profiles each
- Each profile installed via `hermes -p <name> gateway install` (labels `ai.hermes.gateway-<profile>`, `KeepAlive=true`)

## Reproduction

1. Multi-profile macOS install: root gateway + N profile gateways under launchd.
2. Run `hermes update` (any profile; bare root is the common case).
3. Observe: output prints `✓ Restarted ai.hermes.gateway` — root only. `ps -eo pid,etime,command | grep "gateway run"` shows every sibling still on its old start time across updates.
4. Message any sibling profile's agent → its turn crashes.

## Failure signatures (from production logs, two machines)

Small version gap (original incident, v0.16.0, 2026-06-15) — a symbol the new code lazily imports mid-turn:

```
File ".../agent/agent_init.py", line 1196, in init_agent
    from agent.memory_manager import inject_memory_provider_tools as _inject_memory_provider_tools
ImportError: cannot import name 'inject_memory_provider_tools'
             from 'agent.memory_manager' (.../agent/memory_manager.py)
```

The file on disk **does** define the symbol; the process never reloaded it.

Wider gap (recurrence, 2026-07-28, gateways 5 days stale): stale loaded code calling into reloaded modules — note the tracebacks are *garbled* (line numbers resolve to unrelated source lines because the files on disk no longer match the loaded code objects), which is why users report this as "my agent hangs/dies randomly after updates" rather than finding the root cause:

```
TypeError: run_conversation() got an unexpected keyword argument 'persist_user_display_kind'
...
AttributeError: 'TelegramAdapter' object has no attribute 'message_len_fn_for_chat'
```

Both fired 28 seconds after `hermes update` completed, on the first inbound Telegram message.

## Why nothing else compensates

- The launchd branch of the update block checks a single profile-scoped label (`get_launchd_label()`) — by design it can't see siblings.
- The post-restart "manual gateway" sweep can't catch them either: on macOS `_scan_gateway_pids` shells out to `ps -A eww -o pid=,command=`, which BSD `ps` rejects (`ps: illegal argument: eww`, exit 1), so the scan silently returns `[]` on every macOS machine — filed separately as its own issue.

## Root cause

`_cmd_update_impl`'s launchd section restarts `get_launchd_label()` only, while the systemd section iterates `systemctl list-units 'hermes-gateway*'`. Python never re-reads an imported module; only a process restart picks up the pulled code, and launchd `KeepAlive` never restarts a healthy process on its own.

## Relationship to PR #41403

#41403 had the right idea (enumerate `ai.hermes.gateway*.plist`, kickstart siblings) and we confirmed its core logic against a 10-profile fleet at the time (see the reproduction comment there). The automated review found a real defect — it resolves one launchd domain (from the current profile, cached process-wide) and reuses it for every sibling, which breaks mixed `gui/<uid>` / `user/<uid>` fleets (we run one: a profile installed over SSH landed in `user/<uid>`). The branch has since gone stale/unmergeable.

A superseding PR (linked below) rebases the approach onto the current fleet-restart framework, resolves the domain per label, drains siblings via SIGUSR1 like the systemd path, verifies each service on a fresh PID, feeds failures into `_warn_incomplete_gateway_fleet_restart`, and adds the mocked regression tests the review asked for — with co-author credit to #41403's author.

## Workaround until merged

Wrapper script after every update: enumerate `launchctl list | grep ai.hermes.gateway-` and `launchctl kickstart -k <domain>/<label>` each sibling, then verify post-boot logs are ImportError-free. (Happy to share it, but the PR makes it obsolete.)

items.title: macOS: _scan_gateway_pids always returns [] — `ps -A eww` is illegal on BSD ps, manual-gateway sweep is dead code on macOS

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

items.body:
## Summary

`hermes_cli/gateway.py::_scan_gateway_pids` falls back to `ps` when `/proc` is absent — which on macOS is always. The invocation is:

```python
result = subprocess.run(
    ["ps", "-A", "eww", "-o", "pid=,command="], ...
)
if result.returncode != 0:
    return []
```

macOS/BSD `ps` rejects that flag combination outright:

```
$ ps -A eww -o pid=,command=; echo rc=$?
ps: illegal argument: eww
usage: ps [-AaCcEefhjlMmrSTvwXx] ...
rc=1
```

So the scan hits the `returncode != 0` guard and **silently returns `[]` on every macOS machine** — verified on Darwin 25.x with 9 live gateways matching the command-line matcher (`looks_like_gateway_command_line` returns True for their argv; the scan still yields nothing).

On Linux the bug is masked because `/proc` exists and the `ps` fallback rarely runs (and procps tolerates BSD-style mixing anyway).

## Impact

Every macOS consumer of the process-table scan quietly under-reports:

- `hermes update`'s "manual (non-service) gateways" sweep never finds stale manually-run gateways on macOS — they keep running pre-update code (same user-facing symptom as the launchd fleet-restart gap, filed separately).
- `find_gateway_pids(all_profiles=True)` and status paths that rely on the scan to spot gateways with stale/missing PID files can't.

## Fix sketch

Environment variables aren't wanted in the output (the matcher only needs argv), so drop the BSD `e` flag: `ps -Aww -o pid=,command=` — verified working on macOS (returns all gateway processes; `-ww` keeps unlimited width). Optionally assert non-zero output in tests via a fake `ps` to prevent regression.

## Sequencing note

Fixing this scan alone would make the update sweep suddenly *see* launchd-managed sibling gateways and treat them as manual processes (SIGUSR1/SIGTERM + a detached respawn watcher racing launchd's `KeepAlive` respawn → duplicate gateways). The superseding fleet-restart PR (linked) extends `_get_service_pids(all_profiles=True)` to cover every `ai.hermes.gateway*` service, which makes this fix safe to land afterwards. Happy to submit the `ps` fix as a follow-up PR once that merges.

items.title: [Bug]: Desktop Sessions list continuous flicker/jitter while scrolling (Win11; not on Win10)

labels.name: sweeper:risk-platform-windows
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break or behave differently on native Windows

items.body:
https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/acefa5c4-3630-4662-8b58-5a8c58052f16

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/43426218-f1c9-4c5c-8c37-4a13f3b398e1

## Bug Description

Hermes Desktop sidebar **Sessions** list starts continuous jitter/flicker after scrolling down a couple of times. The list looks like it is re-rendering nonstop (virtualizer thrashing), not a one-frame glitch.

Reproduced on **Windows 11**. **Not observed on Windows 10** with the same app/backend.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open Hermes Desktop connected to a backend with a long session history (enough rows for the virtualized recents list; threshold is 25+ sessions).
2. Open the left sidebar **Sessions** list (flat recents with date dividers, e.g. unlabelled head + "Earlier this month").
3. Scroll down a few wheel/trackpad ticks.
4. Observe the list begin continuous jitter/flicker while idle or while continuing to scroll.

## Expected Behavior

Session list scrolls smoothly and stays visually stable after scroll settles. Background session refresh should not visibly thrash the virtualized list.

## Actual Behavior

After a short amount of scrolling, the Sessions list repeatedly jerks/flickers as if endlessly remeasuring/re-rendering. Issue is much more noticeable on Windows 11 than Windows 10 (same product).

## Environment

- App: Hermes Desktop (Electron)
- OS (affected): Windows 11 laptop
- OS (not affected): Windows 10
- Backend/repo commit observed: origin/main as of 2026-07-28 (includes ed6ec0c17 date dividers)
- Related feature commit: ed6ec0c17 — feat(desktop): date dividers in the sessions sidebar (PR #70822)

## Likely cause (code pointers)

Two contributing layers:

### 1) Unmemoized flatRows fed into the virtualizer

In apps/desktop/src/app/chat/sidebar/sessions-section.tsx, displayEntries is memoized, but flatRows is recomputed on every render without useMemo:

    const flatRows: SidebarListRow[] = dateGrouped
      ? groupEntriesByRecency(displayEntries)
      : toSessionRows(displayEntries)

That new array reference is passed into VirtualSessionList (apps/desktop/src/app/chat/sidebar/virtual-session-list.tsx, TanStack react-virtual). Fresh row objects + continuous parent re-renders cause remeasure/layout thrash during scroll.

renderRow / renderListRow / renderRows are also plain inline functions (not useCallback), which amplifies child re-renders.

### 2) Frequent multi-source session list refresh

Sessions store is updated from multiple paths concurrently:

- REST refreshSessions / sidebar aggregator
- WebSocket gateway events → scheduleSessionsRefresh() (~300ms coalesce in use-message-stream)
- Live status poll every 1.5s (LIVE_SESSION_STATUS_POLL_INTERVAL_MS in use-background-sync.ts)

Even with debounce on some paths, parallel sources can still push new sessions references often enough that the unmemoized virtualized list visibly stutters — especially under Windows 11 compositor/smooth-scroll behavior.

## Notes

- This does not appear fixed on current origin/main (still no useMemo on flatRows after the date-dividers feature).
- Nearby historical fixes exist for other jitter/flicker classes (e.g. warm-route resume jitter via double setMessages) but not this sidebar scroll/virtualizer case.
- Win11-only visibility is consistent with the same React thrash being more obvious under Win11 scrolling/compositing, not necessarily a separate Win32-only codepath.

## Suggested fix direction (optional)

1. useMemo for flatRows keyed on displayEntries + dateGrouped
2. useCallback for row render helpers
3. Stronger list-store identity/signature gate so REST/WS/poll no-ops when the sidebar-relevant session signature is unchanged

Happy to attach a short screen recording if useful.

items.title: Handle list-valued assistant content in think-block stripping
items.body:
## Summary
When an OpenAI-compatible/Codex response stores assistant `content` as a list of structured content parts, Hermes can crash during retry/interim-message handling while trying to strip `<think>` blocks.

## Reproduction evidence
In a live CLI session using `openai-codex`/OpenAI-compatible mode, repeated retries reported:

```text
expected string or bytes-like object, got 'list'
```

The stack trace points at `strip_think_blocks` calling `re.sub(...)` on list-valued assistant content from `_interim_assistant_visible_text`.

## Expected behavior
Hermes should normalize structured content parts to visible text before running text-only regex cleanup, ignoring image-only parts.

## Verification
Targeted regression coverage should exercise list-valued content with text and image parts.

items.title: [Bug]: Desktop voice conversation never re-arms mic after normal playback

labels.name: area/streaming
labels.description: Streaming responses: gateway delivery, provider wire

items.body:
## Bug Description

On current `main`, Hermes Desktop Voice Conversation completes the first spoken round trip but does not return to `listening` after the assistant's reply finishes normally. The Voice Conversation UI remains enabled, but the microphone is not re-armed; the user must stop and restart Voice Conversation to speak again.

This is a deterministic regression in the playback-sequence logic added by the streaming/barge-in rewrite in PR #69511. It is distinct from provider latency or microphone permission failure: initial capture, transcription, model response, and TTS playback all succeed.

This is also a follow-up to #51265, which was closed as fixed by PR #69511. The rewrite removes the old delayed re-arm path, but the new sequence comparison suppresses re-arming entirely after normal playback.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run current Hermes Desktop from `main` / Hermes Agent `v0.19.0` at upstream `2cf656f2`.
2. Configure working STT and TTS providers.
3. Start **Voice Conversation** from the Desktop composer.
4. Speak a short prompt and allow transcription/submission to complete.
5. Let the assistant's spoken reply finish normally. Do not press Stop, type over playback, or barge in.
6. Attempt to speak the next turn.

Reproduces on the first completed round trip. Stopping and restarting Voice Conversation temporarily restores the microphone for one more round trip.

## Expected Behavior

After normal TTS completion, Voice Conversation should immediately transition from `speaking` to `listening` and accept the next spoken turn.

An explicit user Stop action should continue to suppress automatic re-arming.

## Actual Behavior

Normal playback completion is classified as though the user explicitly stopped playback. `pendingStartRef.current` is therefore not set, status returns to `idle`, and the microphone never reopens.

## Affected Component

Other — Hermes Desktop (`apps/desktop`), Voice Conversation / streaming TTS playback.

## Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

N/A — native Hermes Desktop.

## Debug Report

Private Nous diagnostics bundle (secret-redacted; Nous staff/allowlisted-moderator access only; auto-deletes after 14 days):

https://support.nousresearch.com/diagnostics/3f6ecf4d-2fc9-46db-91b6-8446791906c3

The bundle is intentionally not hosted on the public paste service because Desktop logs can contain conversation fragments and local paths.

## Operating System

Windows 10 Pro x64, build `10.0.19045.7548`.

## Python Version

`3.11.15`

## Hermes Version

`Hermes Agent v0.19.0 (2026.7.20) · upstream 2cf656f2` (`hermes --version` reports up to date).

## Additional Logs / Traceback

No exception is emitted. Initial microphone acquisition and transcription work. The failure occurs only in the post-playback state transition.

## Root Cause Analysis

`use-voice-conversation.ts` captures the playback sequence **before** starting normal playback:

```ts
// apps/desktop/src/app/chat/composer/hooks/use-voice-conversation.ts
speechStartSequenceRef.current = $voicePlayback.get().sequence
const session = await startSpeechStream({ source: 'voice-conversation' })
```

But `startSpeechStream()` performs normal internal cleanup by calling `stopVoicePlayback()` before opening the new stream:

```ts
// apps/desktop/src/lib/voice-playback.ts
stopVoicePlayback()
setVoicePlaybackState(currentState('preparing', options))
```

`stopVoicePlayback()` unconditionally increments the global sequence:

```ts
export function stopVoicePlayback() {
  sequence += 1
  // ...
}
```

When speech settles, the conversation loop interprets any sequence increase as an explicit user stop:

```ts
const stoppedByUser =
  speechStartSequenceRef.current > 0 &&
  $voicePlayback.get().sequence > speechStartSequenceRef.current

if (enabledRef.current && !stoppedByUser) {
  pendingStartRef.current = true
}
```

Therefore the normal streaming path is guaranteed to evaluate `stoppedByUser === true`:

```text
captured before playback: 7
normal startSpeechStream cleanup: 8
8 > 7 => stoppedByUser
pending mic re-arm => false
```

The whole-text fallback has the same bug: it captures the sequence before calling `playSpeechText()`, and `playSpeechText()` also begins with `stopVoicePlayback()`.

There is currently no Desktop test covering a complete `listening → transcribing → thinking → speaking → listening` cycle. The tests listed in PR #69511 cover backend streaming, chunking, CLI/TUI integration, and provider behavior, but not this renderer state-machine invariant.

## Proposed Fix

Record the playback baseline only **after** the normal internal start/cleanup increment for both paths, so later sequence changes represent an actual external interruption:

- **Streaming path:** set `speechStartSequenceRef.current` after `await startSpeechStream(...)` returns a live session and before awaiting `session.done`.
- **Whole-text fallback:** invoke `playSpeechText(...)`, then capture the post-start playback sequence before awaiting/finalizing that promise.

A more explicit alternative would be for playback APIs to return an instance token or completion reason (`completed` vs `interrupted`) rather than inferring user intent from a global counter.

Please add renderer regression coverage for both streaming and fallback paths:

1. Normal completion sets the next microphone start pending and returns to `listening`.
2. Explicit Stop advances the post-start token and does **not** re-arm.
3. The first and subsequent voice round trips behave identically.
4. Barge-in capture continues to own the microphone without opening a second recorder.

## Are you willing to submit a PR for this?

No checkbox selected; this report provides a verified root cause and proposed test contract.

items.title: Desktop: audio helpers omit profileScoped(), so non-default profiles get the default profile's TTS voice

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Summary

In Hermes Desktop, three audio helpers in `apps/desktop/src/hermes.ts` omit `...profileScoped()`. Because `request.profile` is then `undefined`, Electron routes those calls to the **primary** backend rather than the active profile's, so a user working in a non-default profile gets the **default profile's** ElevenLabs voice.

Everything else about a scoped session behaves correctly — SOUL.md, memory/Honcho peer, skills, sessions and history all follow the selected profile. Only audio doesn't, which makes it present as a voice-config bug rather than a routing one. I spent a while checking `tts.elevenlabs.voice_id` on disk before finding the real cause.

## Affected

`apps/desktop/src/hermes.ts` — `profileScoped()` is spread into 84 call sites. Exactly three omit it, all audio:

| Helper | Endpoint |
|---|---|
| `transcribeAudio` | `/api/audio/transcribe` |
| `speakText` | `/api/audio/speak` |
| `getElevenLabsVoices` | `/api/audio/elevenlabs/voices` |

## Why routing is the right fix

Per `apps/desktop/src/hermes.ts` (~220-229): *"Electron main consumes `request.profile` to pick which backend process serves the call; each pooled backend already has its own `HERMES_HOME`, so no backend change is needed. Null → primary."*

So the server side needs no change — each pooled backend is already correctly homed. `tools/tts_tool.py` resolves TTS config via `_load_tts_config()` → `load_config()` → `get_hermes_home()`, i.e. from whichever backend serves the request. Adding the profile to the request is sufficient.

## Reproduce

1. `hermes profile create researcher`
2. `hermes -p researcher config set tts.elevenlabs.voice_id <a distinct voice>`
3. `hermes -p researcher config get tts.elevenlabs --json` — confirm it differs from `default`
4. In Desktop, open a session **belonging to the `researcher` profile** (i.e. pool-routed, *not* the profile switch that reloads the window) and have it speak.

**Expected:** researcher's voice. **Actual:** default profile's voice.

Note the window-reloading profile switch (`hermes:profile:set`) *does* work, because it re-homes the primary backend — which is a useful diagnostic A/B.

## Patch

```diff
   export function transcribeAudio(dataUrl: string, mimeType?: string): Promise<AudioTranscriptionResponse> {
     return window.hermesDesktop.api<AudioTranscriptionResponse>({
       path: '/api/audio/transcribe',
       method: 'POST',
       body: { data_url: dataUrl, mime_type: mimeType },
-      timeoutMs: audioTranscribeRequestTimeoutMs(dataUrl)
+      timeoutMs: audioTranscribeRequestTimeoutMs(dataUrl),
+      ...profileScoped()
     })
   }

   export function speakText(text: string): Promise<AudioSpeakResponse> {
     return window.hermesDesktop.api<AudioSpeakResponse>({
       path: '/api/audio/speak',
       method: 'POST',
       body: { text },
-      timeoutMs: audioSpeakRequestTimeoutMs(text)
+      timeoutMs: audioSpeakRequestTimeoutMs(text),
+      ...profileScoped()
     })
   }

   export function getElevenLabsVoices(): Promise<ElevenLabsVoicesResponse> {
     return window.hermesDesktop.api<ElevenLabsVoicesResponse>({
-      path: '/api/audio/elevenlabs/voices'
+      path: '/api/audio/elevenlabs/voices',
+      ...profileScoped()
     })
   }
```

## Test

`apps/desktop/src/hermes-profile-scope.test.ts` already states the contract — *"every backend-targeted action helper must carry the active gateway profile"* — but doesn't cover the audio helpers. Suggested addition:

```ts
it('forwards the active profile to audio helpers (speak / transcribe / voices)', () => {
  setApiRequestProfile('researcher')

  void speakText('hello')
  void transcribeAudio('data:audio/webm;base64,AAAA', 'audio/webm')
  void getElevenLabsVoices()

  expect(api.mock.calls).toHaveLength(3)
  for (const call of api.mock.calls) {
    expect(call[0].profile).toBe('researcher')
  }
})
```

Verified locally: fails without the patch (`expected undefined to be 'researcher'`), passes with it. Full file: 4 passed.

## Environment

- Hermes v0.19.0, tag `v2026.7.20` (`3ef6bbd20`), Linux
- Desktop built from source; fix confirmed present in the built bundle
- Multi-profile: `default` / `researcher` / `coder`, each with a distinct `tts.elevenlabs.voice_id`

Happy to open this as a PR if that's easier — the branch is ready.

When /voice tts mode is active, the gateway auto-generates TTS at 1x speed with no way to change it. The text_to_speech tool already supports a speed parameter (0.25–4.0x via edge-tts), but the auto-TTS path in gateway/run.py doesn't read a config value for it.

items.title: Windows: hermes update fails with 'os error 5' on cryptography._rust.pyd

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

labels.name: sweeper:risk-compatibility
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break existing users, config, migrations, defaults, or upgrades

labels.name: sweeper:risk-platform-windows
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break or behave differently on native Windows

items.body:
## Summary

On Windows, running `hermes update` fails with a file lock error when upgrading the `cryptography` package. The error prevents `cryptography` from being installed, causing the update to fall back to ZIP download (which may also fail due to network issues).

## Error Output

```
error: Failed to install: cryptography-48.0.1-cp311-abi3-win_amd64.whl (cryptography==48.0.1)
  Caused by: failed to rename file from ...\venv\Lib\site-packages\cryptography\hazmat\bindings\.tmpXXXXX\_rust.pyd to ...\venv\Lib\site-packages\cryptography\hazmat\bindings\_rust.pyd: 拒绝访问。 (os error 5)
```

## Root Cause

The `_rust.pyd` file within the `cryptography` package is locked by an active Python process (the hermes gateway process `hermes_cli.main gateway run --replace`). Even though the update script claims to pause the gateway, the file remains locked, preventing the pip installer from completing the upgrade.

## Environment

- OS: Windows 11 Enterprise
- Hermes Agent: v0.19.0
- Install method: git
- Install directory: D:\Manager\AppData\Hermes\hermes-agent
- Python: 3.11.15 (venv)
- cryptography before update: 46.0.7
- cryptography target version: 48.0.1

## Workaround

Manually kill all Python processes before running `hermes update`:

```powershell
Get-Process python -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Stop-Process -Force
hermes update --yes
```

If update already failed, manually reinstall cryptography after killing processes:

```bash
./venv/Scripts/python.exe -m pip install --force-reinstall --no-deps cryptography==48.0.1
```

## Suggested Fixes

1. **Ensure gateway is fully stopped before pip install**: The update script should verify the gateway process has actually terminated (not just paused) before attempting pip install. Consider using process termination instead of pause.

2. **Add a retry with file lock detection**: If pip install fails with `os error 5`, the update script should:
   - Wait for the gateway to fully stop
   - Retry the install
   - Or provide a clear error message telling the user to manually kill Python processes

3. **Consider using `--link-mode=copy` on Windows**: The hardlink fallback warning suggests filesystem differences between the cache and target. Setting `UV_LINK_MODE=copy` may reduce edge cases on Windows.

4. **Add Windows-specific file lock handling**: Python on Windows commonly locks loaded DLLs/PYD files. The update process should account for this.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Install hermes-agent on Windows (git install)
2. Run `hermes update` (gateway is running)
3. Observe the cryptography install failure

items.title: [Bug]: Desktop auto-TTS (Read Responses Aloud) toggle active but TTS never fires on API server path

labels.name: sweeper:cannot-reproduce
labels.description: Sweeper: could not reproduce on current main

items.body:
## Bug Description

The Hermes Desktop app exposes a **"Read Responses Aloud"** (auto-speak) toggle in the composer bar and a corresponding section in Settings → Voice. When enabled, the UI indicates that assistant responses should be spoken automatically. However, TTS audio is never generated for responses in the desktop app, even though:

- `voice.auto_tts: true` is set in `config.yaml`
- Edge TTS is configured and functional (`tts.provider: edge`)
- Manual TTS via the `text_to_speech` tool works correctly
- Auto-TTS **does** work on Telegram and other platform adapters

## Root Cause Analysis

The desktop app communicates with Hermes through the **API server adapter** (`gateway/platforms/api_server.py`), which inherits from `BasePlatformAdapter` but does **not** implement the auto-TTS logic present in `gateway/platforms/base.py`.

In `base.py` lines 5513-5535, auto-TTS is gated by:

```python
if (self._should_auto_tts_for_chat(event.source.chat_id)
        and event.message_type == MessageType.VOICE
        ...
```

This logic only fires when:
1. The chat has auto-TTS enabled (via `/voice on` or global `voice.auto_tts`)
2. The incoming message type is `VOICE` (user sent a voice note)

The API server adapter processes messages as raw HTTP/SSE requests without the `MessageType.VOICE` event structure used by platform adapters. Consequently, the auto-TTS code path is completely bypassed for desktop sessions.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open Hermes Desktop app
2. Ensure **Read Responses Aloud** is enabled (speaker icon in composer bar is active)
3. Send any text message to the agent
4. Observe that the response is text-only — no audio is generated or played

## Expected Behavior

When auto-speak is enabled in the desktop app, every assistant response should trigger TTS generation and playback, matching the behavior on Telegram when a user sends a voice note.

## Actual Behavior

No TTS audio is generated for any response in the desktop app, regardless of the auto-speak toggle state.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent version: 0.19.0 (2026-07-21)
- Desktop app build: 2026-07-27T15:13:14
- macOS 26.3.1
- TTS provider: Edge TTS (`en-US-ChristopherNeural`)
- STT: Local faster-whisper (functional — voice notes are transcribed correctly)

## Evidence

1. **Config confirms auto_tts enabled:**

```yaml
voice:
  auto_tts: true
tts:
  provider: edge
```

2. **Desktop UI shows toggle active** (speaker icon enabled in composer bar)

3. **Manual TTS works** — calling the `text_to_speech` tool generates and plays audio correctly

4. **API server adapter has zero TTS references:**

```bash
grep -n "auto_tts\|_auto_tts\|voice_mode\|tts" gateway/platforms/api_server.py
# Returns: no matches
```

5. **Platform adapters (Telegram, Discord) implement auto-TTS** in `base.py` with the `MessageType.VOICE` gate, but this code path is unreachable from the API server.

## Suggested Fix

Implement auto-TTS in the API server adapter by either:

1. **Adding TTS generation to the response pipeline** in `api_server.py` after the agent response is complete, gated by the `voice.auto_tts` config value
2. **Emitting a synthetic `MessageType.VOICE` event** for desktop voice-input sessions so the existing `base.py` auto-TTS logic fires
3. **Adding a dedicated desktop voice mode** that the API server adapter can check and act on

The cleanest approach is likely option 1 — generate TTS in the API server response handler when `voice.auto_tts` is true, using the same `text_to_speech_tool` utility that platform adapters use.

## Additional Context

This was discovered while troubleshooting why voice responses worked on Telegram but not in the desktop app. The desktop app is the primary interface, so this gap significantly impacts usability for users who rely on audio feedback.

items.title: Desktop leaves timed-out subagents stuck as running

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
## Summary

Hermes Desktop can permanently show timed-out delegated tasks as active in the composer status stack. In the observed incident, the expanded panel said **“9 Subagents”** and rendered nine rows as running even though all nine matching durable task results were terminal `timeout` results and `delegation.status` reported no active workers.

This is not just stale process state: the renderer normalizes an unrecognized terminal status to `running`, and later cleanup intentionally preserves running rows.

## Environment

- Hermes Desktop footer: `v0.19.0`
- Running source commit: `2b0fb72acae67f51652de5c51db556bc15a68f0e`
- Reconfirmed against current `origin/main`: `9b6d91045cc821428455939f740519f5099a6dc5` (the same status-normalization gap is still present)
- Windows 11 Pro, 64-bit, build 26200

## Reproduction

1. Start one or more background delegations from Desktop.
2. Let the worker timeout so the backend emits a terminal `subagent.complete` payload with `status: "timeout"`.
3. Observe the composer’s Agents/Subagents status group.
4. Send another message or allow the turn to finish so normal status pruning runs.

### Actual

The timed-out rows remain in the active Subagents group indefinitely, showing their last tool labels and running affordances. The UI can claim that multiple subagents are active even when no subagent processes exist.

### Expected

A timeout is terminal. It should render as failed/timed out, cease appearing in the active status stack, and be eligible for normal terminal-row pruning.

## Root cause

The backend legitimately uses terminal statuses including `timeout` (and one error path uses `error`) in `tools/delegate_tool.py`.

In `apps/desktop/src/store/subagents.ts`, `asStatus()` currently recognizes only:

- `completed`
- `failed`
- `interrupted`
- `queued`

Every other value falls through to `running`. Therefore, a `subagent.complete` event carrying `timeout` (or `error`, or any future terminal status) is converted to `running`.

`pruneFinishedSessionSubagents()` then keeps `running`/`queued` rows by design, and `composerStatusRows()` includes them in the active composer stack. The combination makes timeout rows effectively immortal.

## Proposed fix (validated locally)

Make terminal-event normalization fail closed:

- Keep recognized statuses as-is.
- Map `cancelled`/`canceled` to `interrupted` for compatibility.
- For any unrecognized status on `subagent.complete`, return `failed` rather than `running`.
- Keep unknown nonterminal progress statuses as `running` for forward compatibility.

A table-driven regression was added for backend terminal values `timeout`, `error`, and an unknown future terminal value. Each now becomes `failed`, clears `currentTool`, and is removed by `pruneFinishedSessionSubagents()`.

Validation on the local fix:

- `src/store/subagents.test.ts`: 13/13 passed
- Tracked Desktop UI suite: 2,529 passed, 1 skipped
- Production Desktop build: passed
- `git diff --check`: passed

(The checkout also contained one unrelated untracked test file with four pre-existing failures; it was excluded from the tracked-suite verification and was not modified.)

## User impact

- Misleading active-agent count and spinner state
- Users may believe workers are still consuming tokens or compute
- Stop/cleanup investigations target processes that no longer exist
- The stale rows can accumulate across multiple timed-out batches

## Privacy

The original screenshot and task titles are intentionally not attached because they contain project-specific task text and local paths. This report includes only aggregate counts and source-level behavior; no session IDs, delegation IDs, local user paths, credentials, tokens, prompts, or task contents are included.

items.title: [Bug]: local-ollama-setup docs contradict themselves on gemma2:27b tool-calling support
items.body:
## Summary

`website/docs/guides/local-ollama-setup.md` gives two opposite answers about whether `gemma2:27b` supports tool calling. Which answer a reader gets depends on which section of the same page they land on.

## Evidence

Line numbers from `main`, verified today against `raw.githubusercontent.com` (317-line file).

**Says no** (model table, L62):

```
| `gemma2:27b` | ~16 GB | 20+ GB | No | Conversational tasks, no tool use |
```

**Says no** ("Which model should I use?" table, L141):

```
| File edits, code, terminal commands | `gemma4:31b` | Only model with reliable tool calling |
```

**Says yes** ("Model doesn't follow tool calls" troubleshooting, L283):

```
- **Use a bigger model** — `gemma4:31b` or `gemma2:27b` handle tool calls much better than 3B/7B models.
```

L283 recommends `gemma2:27b` as the remedy for a model that ignores tool calls, while L62 says that model has no tool use at all and L141 says `gemma4:31b` is the *only* model with reliable tool calling.

Secondary point in the same section: L281 frames the symptom as "Smaller models (3B, 7B)", but 3B and 7B appear nowhere else in the guide. The smallest model in its own table is `gemma2:9b`.

## Why it matters

This is the entry-point guide for running Hermes at zero API cost, so it is often read before a hardware decision rather than after. The two answers point at different RAM budgets: 24+ GB for `gemma4:31b` versus 20+ GB for `gemma2:27b`, per the guide's own table.

A reader who follows L283 lands exactly on the failure mode L67 warns about: "Models without tool-call support can only chat; they can't take actions."

## Suggested fix

If the table is authoritative, L283 should stop naming `gemma2:27b`:

```diff
-- **Use a bigger model** — `gemma4:31b` or `gemma2:27b` handle tool calls much better than 3B/7B models.
+- **Use a model with tool-call support**: see the model table above. Of the listed models, only `gemma4:31b` has reliable tool calling.
```

Aligning L281 with the guide's own model range (`gemma2:9b` rather than 3B/7B) would help too.

If instead `gemma2:27b` does support tool calling in practice, then L62 and L141 are the lines that need correcting.

I am happy to send a PR once a maintainer confirms which direction is correct. The docs alone do not determine it, and guessing would just move the contradiction somewhere else.

items.title: [Bug]: Relay scope stack corruption — "scope handle is not at the top of the stack" during turn finalization

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

items.body:
## Version
- Hermes Agent: 0.19.0
- nemo_relay: 0.6.0

## Symptom
```
WARNING [<session_id>] agent.relay_runtime: Hermes Relay turn finalization failed
RuntimeError: invalid argument: scope handle is not at the top of the stack
  File ".../agent/relay_runtime.py", line 644, in end_turn
  File ".../agent/relay_runtime.py", line 217, in run_in_session
  File ".../agent/relay_runtime.py", line 213, in invoke
  File ".../nemo_relay/scope.py", line 144, in pop
```

## Details
The error fires at `relay_runtime.py:644` during `end_turn()` when calling `lease.host.run_in_session(...)` with `relay.scope.pop(turn.handle)`. The nemo_relay scope stack rejects the pop because the handle is not at the top — meaning something pushed a scope that was never popped, or pops are happening out of order.

## Occurrence pattern
- 3 occurrences across 3 distinct sessions within ~33 minutes (07:37–08:10 UTC, 2026-07-29)
- Sessions affected: `20260723_024537_95c0e6f7`, `20260728_233758_0c6b3c0d`, `20260729_070054_b8452262`
- Not continuous — no recurrence after the 08:10 event

## Impact
- Exception is caught (recoverable) — logged as WARNING, not ERROR
- Turn finalization cleanup may be incomplete (scope not popped properly)
- Next turn starts fresh, so no persistent session corruption observed
- Unclear if this causes a slow scope leak over long-running sessions

## Likely cause
Some code path pushes a scope onto the session stack without corresponding pop, or pops in wrong order. The fact that it happens at `end_turn` (not mid-operation) suggests cleanup ordering rather than live misuse.

## Related
Discovered alongside a separate Mnemosyne config issue (`tools: None` causing tool schema load warnings — fixed by removing the line). The two may be correlated if a Mnemosyne tool failure triggers an unusual scope path that leaves the stack in a bad state.

items.title: Kanban worker stopped by a provider wall exits 0 and is auto-blocked as a protocol violation, the one classification that forbids a retry

labels.name: sweeper:cannot-reproduce
labels.description: Sweeper: could not reproduce on current main

items.body:
Related to #46593 and #27924, which report the same `clean_exit` classification from different causes: a crash before the first API call, and a worker completing silently. This one is a third cause with a different remedy, and the remedy already exists in the codebase. Closing as a duplicate is fine if you disagree, but the discriminator below is not covered by either.

v0.18.0 already distinguishes a transient provider failure from a task
failure, and does it well. `hermes_cli/kanban_db.py::_classify_worker_exit`
maps `KANBAN_RATE_LIMIT_EXIT_CODE` (75) to a `rate_limited` exit, and
`detect_crashed_workers` then releases the card back to `ready` **without**
incrementing the failure counter, so a long quota window cannot trip the
circuit breaker. That is exactly the right behaviour.

The problem is which runs can reach it. In `cli.py` the worker's exit code is
decided by:

```python
_exit_code = 0
if isinstance(result, dict) and result.get("failed"):
    _exit_code = 1
    if os.environ.get("HERMES_KANBAN_TASK") and result.get("failure_reason") in ("rate_limit", "billing"):
        _exit_code = _RL_CODE
sys.exit(_exit_code)
```

`failure_reason` is only set where `agent/conversation_loop.py` returns
`failed: True` after exhausting API retries. When the provider walls the run
but the turn still ends normally — the model produces a final assistant
message explaining that it was rate-limited, rather than the loop raising —
`result["failed"]` is falsy. The process exits **0** with the card still
`running`, and `_classify_worker_exit` returns `clean_exit`.

`clean_exit` is documented as a protocol violation ("worker exited without
calling `kanban_complete` / `kanban_block` ... should be auto-blocked
immediately — retrying will just loop"), and the test suite names the case it
is meant for: an agent that answered conversationally instead of calling a
terminal tool. For that case the classification is right.

For a provider wall it is the worst possible outcome. The most retryable
situation there is gets the one classification that forbids a retry, and the
card is blocked until a human unblocks it. The information needed to tell the
two apart exists inside the run: the same conversation that ended
conversationally contains the provider errors that caused it.

Reproduced on 2026-07-28, twice in four minutes, on two independent cards. The run
log ends with the agent rendering an ordinary assistant message:

```
API call failed after 3 retries: HTTP 429: You exceeded your current quota,
please check your plan and billing details.
* Quota exceeded for metric: generativelanguage.googleapis.

Session:        <id>
Duration:       52s
Messages:       25 (1 user, 24 tool calls)
```

The process exits 0 and the dispatcher records:

```
protocol_violation {'pid': ..., 'exit_code': 0}
gave_up {'failures': 2, 'effective_limit': 1, 'limit_source': 'dispatcher',
         'error': 'worker exited cleanly (rc=0) without calling kanban_complete
                   or kanban_block — protocol violation'}
```

Both cards went to `blocked` and stayed there. Nothing in that run was a protocol
violation in the sense the classifier means: the agent did not answer
conversationally instead of using its tools. It made 24 tool calls and then lost
every model it had.

The chain was: primary returned HTTP 429 "the usage limit has been reached", the
runtime switched to a fallback, and the fallback returned HTTP 429 quota
exhausted. A subscription limit and a free-tier quota in one run, and the outcome
was the one classification that forbids the retry which would have fixed it.

Re-checked on v0.19.0 (2026.7.20, commit 3ef6bbd2): the exit-code branch quoted above is
unchanged, and `clean_exit` is still classified as a protocol violation.

Earlier occurrences on the same deployment, 2026-07-21 and 2026-07-22, matched this
shape but their transcripts are gone: the per-task worker log is overwritten by the
successful rerun, which is why this took a month to capture.

Suggested fix, in order of preference:

- classify a `clean_exit` whose run recorded terminal provider errors as
  `rate_limited` rather than `protocol_violation`, so the existing requeue path
  applies; or
- let the turn surface "I stopped because of the provider" even when it does
  not raise, so `failure_reason` is set and the existing exit-code branch does
  the rest; or
- at minimum, record on the blocked card which of the two situations was
  detected. Today both produce the same card and the same message, and an
  operator cannot tell a model that misbehaved from a provider that was down.

Version: v0.18.0 (2026.7.1), re-verified on v0.19.0 (2026.7.20).

items.title: Feature Request: patch_history + content_type for skill/memory metadata

labels.name: duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

items.body:
## Summary

Two metadata enhancements that would improve skill lifecycle management and memory optimization for long-running agents:

## 1. `patch_history` in Skill Metadata (`.usage.json`)

**Current state:** Skills track `patch_count` (aggregate counter) but not per-patch history. Users who want per-patch tracking must implement their own workaround (cronjob + `.patch_history.jsonl`).

**Proposal:** Add optional `patch_history` array to `.usage.json` skill entries:
```json
{
  "skill_name": {
    "patch_count": 45,
    "patch_history": [
      {"timestamp": "2026-07-28T10:15:00Z", "lines_changed": 12, "reason": "Fixed pitfall X"},
      ...
    ]
  }
}
```

**Use cases:**
- Composite fragmentation detection (patch_count + knowledge_signal thresholds)
- Skill lifecycle management (identify churn-heavy skills for refactor)
- Curiosity-driven analysis (which skills evolve fastest?)

## 2. `content_type` Classification in Memory

**Current state:** Memory entries are flat text strings. No structured classification of content type.

**Proposal:** Add optional `content_type` field to memory entries:
```json
{
  "content": "RN 0.81: codegen BEFORE pod install",
  "content_type": "rule"
}
```

Types: `rule`, `preference`, `fact`, `pointer`, `procedure`

**Use cases:**
- Meta-memory optimization (route different content types to different storage layers)
- Memory budget management (prioritize rules over facts when trimming)
- Cross-layer consistency checks

## Context

Both features emerged from running Hermes as a long-lived agent (3+ months, 140+ skills, 4-layer memory architecture). These would reduce reliance on custom workarounds and enable better native tooling for skill/memory management.
