items.title: Gateway /resume numbered list doesn't recover origin-less sessions from state.db

labels.name: sweeper:cannot-reproduce
labels.description: Sweeper: could not reproduce on current main

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
## Problem

When `sessions.json` (the routing map) is lost or partially rebuilt after a crash, the `/resume` numbered list is reconstructed via `_recover_session_from_db` in `gateway/session.py`. This recovery path only fires when `entry.origin is set`:

```python
if entry.origin is not None:
    recovered_entry = self._recover_session_from_db(...)
```

Many sessions (particularly older ones, or those created before the `origin` field existed) have `origin=None`. These sessions are silently pruned from the routing map and never appear in the `/resume` numbered list, even though their content is fully intact in `state.db`.

## Impact

`/resume <session_id>` works (direct DB lookup), but `/resume` (numbered list) misses sessions without origin. Users have to know the session ID to resume.

## Proposed fix

Add a fallback in `_prune_stale_sessions_locked` (or in the `/resume` list builder in `gateway/slash_commands.py`) that recovers origin-less sessions by direct `session_id` lookup against `state.db`, independent of the origin-based `_recover_session_from_db` path.

The recovery should:
1. Check if the session exists in `state.db` via `get_session(session_id)`
2. If it exists and has a recoverable `end_reason`, rebuild the routing entry
3. Make it appear in the `/resume` numbered list

## Context

- Related to #71916 (crash-interrupted session recovery) and #73320 (crash marker fix)
- Discovered during hardening of #73320 — an initial attempt to fix this in the pruning path rebuilt dead sessions instead of finding newer live ones, so it needs the correct code path (the list builder, not the pruner)
- Low urgency: the root cause of routing map loss (Proxmox fsfreeze SIGTERMs) is now eliminated, but this gap still affects any future crash scenario

items.title: [Desktop Critical] Queued messages leak across sessions — switching tabs auto-sends pending input to wrong session

labels.name: duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
## Bug Description
Hermes Desktop chat has a critical message routing bug: **queued messages from the current session get posted to a different session when the user switches sessions** on the Desktop UI.

This causes content cross-contamination — messages intended for Session A end up in Session B's history.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Open Hermes Desktop
2. Start typing a message in Session A (do NOT send yet — message stays queued in input box)
3. Switch to Session B in the sidebar
4. The queued message from Session A **automatically posts/sends to Session B**
5. Session B now contains Session A's unsent message

## Expected Behavior
- Queued/unsent messages should stay bound to their original session
- Switching sessions should NOT trigger sending of pending input
- Each session's input buffer should be isolated

## Actual Behavior
- Typing in Session A → switch to Session B → message auto-sends to Session B
- Session history corruption: foreign messages appear in wrong session
- User loses track of which message belongs to which conversation

## Environment
- Hermes Agent v0.19.0 (upstream 477c08b4)
- Docker install on Linux 6.8.0-136-generic x86_64
- Python 3.13.5
- Profile: default
- Related bug: #74109 (Desktop session list only shows pinned sessions)

## Impact
**HIGH** — Data integrity violation. Users cannot trust session isolation. Conversation history becomes unreliable when multiple sessions are used.

## Root Cause Hypothesis
Desktop client shares a single input buffer/component across session tabs instead of maintaining per-session input state. When tab switches, the buffer flushes to the newly-active session.

items.title: [Bug]: Session hygiene compression cooldown is in-memory only — restarts re-trigger the same failing compression, wedging session storage

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

labels.name: sweeper:risk-message-delivery
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may drop, duplicate, misroute, or suppress messages

labels.name: area/memory
labels.description: Memory subsystem: store, providers, sync, background reviews

items.body:
## Bug Description

The **session hygiene** background compression path tracks its per-session failure cooldown in an **in-memory dict** (`self._hygiene_compression_failure_cooldowns`) on the gateway process. When the gateway restarts, that dict is gone, so the next inbound message immediately re-triggers compression on the same session that just failed.

Meanwhile, the state DB already has a dedicated persistent column (`sessions.compression_failure_cooldown_until`) and full read/write/clear methods (`record_compression_failure_cooldown` / `get_compression_failure_cooldown` / `clear_compression_failure_cooldown` in `hermes_state.py`). Those persistent methods are used by the **in-conversation** compression path (`agent/context_compressor.py`) but are **not** used by the **session hygiene** path in `gateway/run.py`. The two paths disagree on durability.

The concrete user-visible symptom: when compression fails repeatedly on a large session (e.g. the configured aux compression model returns 403 or times out), the session storage write path gets wedged and the user sees:

```
⚠️ No reply: the turn was stopped because session storage could not be written
(the transcript would have been lost on restart). Check disk space / permissions
for the state DB, then send your message again.
```

…on every message, including in **other** sessions, because the failing compression holds the write fence. Restarting the gateway does **not** recover — it clears the in-memory cooldown and the cycle repeats.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure `compression.enabled: true` and an auxiliary compression model (e.g. a paid/coded provider).
2. Let one session accumulate messages past `compression.hygiene_hard_message_limit` (default 400). In my case a long-running gateway session hit ~3000 messages in `state.db` while the `sessions.message_count` metadata lagged at ~428.
3. Make the configured aux compression model unavailable — e.g. the provider returns `HTTP 403: You've reached your usage limit for this billing cycle`, or the summary call times out.
4. Send any message to the gateway. Session hygiene detects the oversized session and triggers compression.
5. Compression fails (403 / timeout). The write fence it holds blocks `append_message` for concurrent turns.
6. Observe repeated `Session DB append_message failed: Session '…' is being compressed by another writer` warnings, and the user-facing `⚠️ No reply: the turn was stopped because session storage could not be written` error.
7. **Restart the gateway.** The in-memory cooldown dict is reset to `{}`. The very next inbound message re-triggers compression on the same oversized session, fails again, and re-wedges storage. The session is never retired — it stays `ended_at=NULL, archived=0` forever and is retried on every gateway boot.

## Expected Behavior

The compression-failure cooldown for session hygiene should be **persisted to the state DB** using the existing `compression_failure_cooldown_until` column and the existing `record_/get_/clear_compression_failure_cooldown` methods — exactly as the in-conversation compression path already does. After a restart, a session whose compression is in cooldown should be skipped for the cooldown's remaining duration rather than re-attempted immediately.

Separately, a session that has failed compression N times (or whose `hygiene_hard_message_limit` trip can never succeed because the aux model is structurally unavailable) should be **auto-retired** (marked `ended`/`archived`) rather than retried forever.

## Actual Behavior

- Session hygiene cooldown lives only in `self._hygiene_compression_failure_cooldowns` (a process-local dict).
- `record_compression_failure_cooldown` / `get_compression_failure_cooldown` (the DB-backed methods in `hermes_state.py`) are **never called** from the session hygiene path.
- Every gateway restart zeroes the cooldown and re-triggers the same failing compression.
- The failing compression holds a write fence (`CompressionCommitFence`) that blocks `append_message` on concurrent turns, surfacing as `session storage could not be written` to the end user — including in unrelated sessions.
- The oversized session is never automatically retired; manual DB surgery (`UPDATE sessions SET ended_at=…, end_reason='agent_close', archived=1 WHERE id=…`) was required to break the loop.

### Relevant logs

From `gateway.log` (repeating across restarts):

```
INFO    Session hygiene: 428 messages, ~138,812 tokens (actual) — auto-compressing (threshold: 85% of 262,144 = 222,822 tokens)
INFO    Session hygiene compression for session 20260729_094814_b31f2ac6 still streaming after 30s (last progress 1.1s ago) — extending wait (ceiling 600s)
INFO    Session hygiene compression for session 20260729_094814_b31f2ac6 still streaming after 60s (last progress 1.8s ago) — extending wait (ceiling 600s)
INFO    Session hygiene compression for session 20260729_094814_b31f2ac6 still streaming after 90s (last progress 12.3s ago) — extending wait (ceiling 600s)
WARNING Session hygiene compression for session 20260729_094814_b31f2ac6 made no progress for 42.3s (total wait 120.0s, ceiling 600.0s); continuing without compression
WARNING Session hygiene auto-compress failed:
WARNING Session DB append_message failed: Session '20260729_094814_b31f2ac6' is being compressed by another writer
```

The same sequence replays after every gateway restart, with a fresh cooldown window each time (confirming the cooldown is not surviving the restart).

## Code Location

The in-memory cooldown (session hygiene path) — `gateway/run.py:13698-13712`:

```python
if _needs_compress:
    _cooldowns = getattr(self, "_hygiene_compression_failure_cooldowns", None)
    if _cooldowns is None:
        _cooldowns = {}
        self._hygiene_compression_failure_cooldowns = _cooldowns
    _cooldown_key = session_entry.session_id
    _cooldown_until = float(_cooldowns.get(_cooldown_key) or 0.0)
    if _cooldown_until > time.time():
        logger.info(
            "Session hygiene: skipping compression for %s; "
            "previous failure cooldown active for %.1fs",
            _cooldown_key, max(0.0, _cooldown_until - time.time()),
        )
        _needs_compress = False
```

The unused persistent mechanism:

- Schema: `hermes_state.py:1282` — `compression_failure_cooldown_until REAL` column on `sessions`.
- Writers: `hermes_state.py:4793-4816` — `record_compression_failure_cooldown(session_id, cooldown_until, error)`.
- Reader: `hermes_state.py:4818-4853` — `get_compression_failure_cooldown(session_id)`.
- Clear: `hermes_state.py:4855-4866` — `clear_compression_failure_cooldown(session_id)`.

The in-conversation path (`agent/context_compressor.py:1757+`) already uses these DB-backed methods. The hygiene path does not.

## Suggested Fix

1. In the session hygiene path, replace the in-memory `_hygiene_compression_failure_cooldowns` dict with calls to `record_compression_failure_cooldown` / `get_compression_failure_cooldown` so the cooldown survives restarts.
2. On compression failure in the hygiene path, call `record_compression_failure_cooldown(...)` with the same semantics the in-conversation path uses.
3. On compression success (or on session end), call `clear_compression_failure_cooldown(...)`.
4. Consider auto-retiring a session (mark `ended`/`archived`) after N consecutive hygiene compression failures, so a structurally-uncompressible session doesn't wedge the gateway indefinitely.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent: **v0.19.0 (v2026.7.20)** — `upstream 0f64557c`
- OS: macOS 26.5 (Apple Silicon, M4)
- Python: 3.11.15
- Multi-profile gateway (feishu adapter)
- Aux compression model: configured to a paid provider that returned 403 for the billing cycle; fallback chain present but the primary's 30s timeout fired first.
- `compression.enabled: true`, `threshold: 0.8`, `hygiene_hard_message_limit: 400`

items.body:
### Bug Description

## Environment
 
- **Hermes Agent:** v0.19.0 (2026.7.20), upstream commit `46c7a407`
- **Install method:** Docker (`nousresearch/hermes-agent:latest`)
- **Host OS:** Ubuntu 24.04 LTS (6.8.0-136-generic), Hostinger KVM4 VPS
- **Python:** 3.13.5
- **OpenAI SDK:** 2.24.0
## Summary
 
The Telegram gateway hangs indefinitely at `Connecting to Telegram (attempt 1/8)…` immediately after `Discovering Telegram API fallback IPs via DNS-over-HTTPS…`. No timeout fires, no crash, no further output — the process sits silently until manually killed.
 
This matches the behavior described in #63309, which was closed as fixed via PR #64370 (thread-based wall-clock deadline on `Application.initialize()` + unbinding DoH fallback-IP discovery from the blocking system resolver). However, the fix code is confirmed present in my running image and the issue still reproduces.
 
## Diagnostic evidence
 
### 1. Bot token is valid
 
Direct curl to Telegram's Bot API using the same token succeeds:
 
```
$ curl https://api.telegram.org/bot<token>/getMe
{"ok":true,"result":{"id":<id>,"is_bot":true,"first_name":"Kelpie","username":"kelpiethehorse_bot",...}}
```
 
### 2. Network connectivity is clean from both host and container
 
```
$ curl -I https://api.telegram.org
HTTP/2 302
server: nginx/1.30.1
...
 
$ docker run --rm curlimages/curl -I https://api.telegram.org
HTTP/2 302
server: nginx/1.30.1
...
```
 
Both return successfully — no DNS failure, no timeout, no firewall blocking.
 
### 3. Fix code from PR #64370 is present in the running image
 
```
$ docker run --rm --entrypoint sh nousresearch/hermes-agent -c "grep -r '_await_with_thread_deadline' /opt/hermes/ 2>/dev/null | head -5"
/opt/hermes/plugins/platforms/telegram/adapter.py:async def _await_with_thread_deadline(awaitable, timeout: float, *, on_abandon=None):
/opt/hermes/plugins/platforms/telegram/adapter.py:                    await _await_with_thread_deadline(
```
 
The function `_await_with_thread_deadline` described in teknium1's closing comment on #63309 exists and is referenced in `adapter.py`.
 
### 4. Image is freshly pulled
 
```
$ docker image inspect nousresearch/hermes-agent:latest --format='{{.Created}}'
2026-07-23T02:16:03.330678723Z
```
 
Multiple fresh pulls were tested across different builds (upstream hashes `8a21df18` and `46c7a407`), all reproduce identically.
 
### 5. Reproduced across multiple configurations
 
| Variable tested | Result |
|---|---|
| Terminal backend: Docker | Hangs at attempt 1/8 |
| Terminal backend: Local (`-e TERMINAL_ENV=local`) | Hangs at attempt 1/8 |
| Token via .env file | Hangs at attempt 1/8 |
| Token via `-e TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN=<token>` (bypassing file entirely) | Hangs at attempt 1/8 |
| Fresh install (wiped `~/.hermes`, re-ran setup wizard) | Hangs at attempt 1/8 |
| Multiple image pulls (different upstream commits) | Hangs at attempt 1/8 |
| `curl getMe` with same token | Succeeds immediately |
| `.env` file inspected with `cat -A` for hidden chars | Clean, no `^M` or encoding issues |
 
### 6. Token was not the issue
 
Initial `curl` test using `grep/cut` extraction from the `.env` file returned a 404, which appeared to indicate an invalid token. However, manually pasting the same token into the curl command returned `{"ok":true}`. This suggests something in the extraction (likely `cut -d=` truncating a token containing `=`) caused a false negative — the token itself was always valid.
 
## Additional observations
 
- SQLite WAL-corruption warnings appear in gateway logs (SQLite 3.46.1 vs recommended 3.51.3+) — unrelated to the hang but present in every run.
- The `ddgs` (DuckDuckGo) search package fails to install during setup (`pip not available and ensurepip failed`) — also unrelated but noted for completeness.
- Direct CLI chat mode (`docker run -it --rm -v ~/.hermes:/opt/data nousresearch/hermes-agent`) works correctly, confirming the agent, model connection, and general container health are fine. However, even in CLI mode, the Telegram adapter attempts to connect in the background and hangs identically.``

### Steps to Reproduce

## Reproduction steps
 
```bash
mkdir -p ~/.hermes
 
# Pre-populate credentials
cat > ~/.hermes/.env << 'EOF'
OPENROUTER_API_KEY=<key>
TERMINAL_ENV=docker
TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN=<valid_token>
TELEGRAM_ALLOWED_USERS=<numeric_id>
EOF
 
# Run setup wizard
docker run -it --rm -v ~/.hermes:/opt/data nousresearch/hermes-agent setup
 
# Start gateway
docker run -it --rm -v ~/.hermes:/opt/data -p 127.0.0.1:8642:8642 nousresearch/hermes-agent gateway run
 
# Hangs here:
# WARNING [Telegram] Discovering Telegram API fallback IPs via DNS-over-HTTPS…
# WARNING [Telegram] Connecting to Telegram (attempt 1/8)…
```

### Expected Behavior

## Expected behavior
 
Gateway should either connect to Telegram successfully (token is valid, network is reachable) or fail with a meaningful error and advance through retry attempts. The wall-clock deadline from PR #64370 should fire and prevent the indefinite hang.

### Actual Behavior

## Actual behavior
 
Gateway hangs indefinitely at attempt 1/8. No timeout fires. No retry. No error output. Process must be killed manually.

### Affected Component

Gateway (Telegram/Discord/Slack/WhatsApp)

N/A

Ubuntu 24.04 LTS (6.8.0-136-generic)

0.19.0 (2026.7.20), upstream commit 46c7a407

items.title: [Bug]: Desktop — the completed-unread green dot never clears for a session open as a tile
items.body:
## Summary

A session that finishes while unfocused gets the steady green "completed, unread" dot. That dot is only ever cleared by `setSelectedStoredSessionId`, which is the *main* thread's selection. A session open as a tile is by construction never the main selection, so its green dot has no clear path at all: focusing the tile, reading the completed response, and interacting with it all leave the dot green until the app restarts or the session is pulled back into main.

The same mismatch has a second face: a tile that finishes *while the user is watching it* is still marked unread, because the mark test compares against the main selection rather than the focused session.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open conversation A as a session tile and conversation B in the main thread.
2. Start a turn in A.
3. Focus B while A completes. A gets the steady green completed-unread dot.
4. Click A's tile tab (or click A in the sidebar, which fronts the existing tile).

Expected: the tile is fronted, the completed response is on screen, and the dot returns to the idle project color.

Actual: the tile is fronted and the response is visible, but the dot stays green. Nothing short of closing the tile and reopening A into the main thread clears it.

Variant, no background step needed: open A as a tile, keep the tile focused, and run a turn to completion. The dot turns green as it finishes, with A visible and focused the whole time.

## Root cause

Only two sites write `$unreadFinishedSessionIds` (plus a wholesale wipe on gateway switch), and both key off `$selectedStoredSessionId`:

- Mark, [`session-states.ts:172-181`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/41a07f5b8451f88a8b8b5adfc0cfdc2ada0a1f90/apps/desktop/src/store/session-states.ts#L172-L181): on a busy → idle transition, add the id if `storedId !== $selectedStoredSessionId.get()`.
- Clear, [`session.ts:436-444`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/41a07f5b8451f88a8b8b5adfc0cfdc2ada0a1f90/apps/desktop/src/store/session.ts#L436-L444): `setSelectedStoredSessionId` drops the newly selected id from the set.

Tiles and main selection are mutually exclusive by design. `use-session-actions` says so directly in a comment at [`index.ts:561-563`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/41a07f5b8451f88a8b8b5adfc0cfdc2ada0a1f90/apps/desktop/src/app/session/hooks/use-session-actions/index.ts#L561-L563), a session is either the main thread or a tile and never both, and `openSessionTile` refuses to tile the selected session. So for a tiled session, the clear condition is unreachable and the mark condition is always true.

The tile-focus path does not compensate. [`focusOpenSession`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/41a07f5b8451f88a8b8b5adfc0cfdc2ada0a1f90/apps/desktop/src/store/session-states.ts#L604-L628) reveals the pane, notes the active group, and returns `'tile'` without touching unread state, and [`open-session.ts:74`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/41a07f5b8451f88a8b8b5adfc0cfdc2ada0a1f90/apps/desktop/src/app/open-session.ts#L74) / [`:87`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/41a07f5b8451f88a8b8b5adfc0cfdc2ada0a1f90/apps/desktop/src/app/open-session.ts#L87) correctly return early on a tile hit, so no navigation or selection change follows to clear it as a side effect.

[`SessionStatusDot`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/41a07f5b8451f88a8b8b5adfc0cfdc2ada0a1f90/apps/desktop/src/app/chat/session-status-dot.tsx#L122) reads the set directly, so both the sidebar row and the tile's own tab keep rendering green.

## Suggested fix

The store already has the right notion of "the session the user is looking at": [`$focusedStoredSessionId`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/41a07f5b8451f88a8b8b5adfc0cfdc2ada0a1f90/apps/desktop/src/store/session-states.ts#L701-L709) resolves the active zone's tile, falling back to the main selection. Both unread sites should key off that instead of the selection alone:

1. Mark: skip the unread mark when `storedId === $focusedStoredSessionId.get()`. Fixes the "goes green while you watch it" variant.
2. Clear: add a narrow `clearUnreadFinishedSession(storedSessionId)` in `session.ts` and drive it from a `$focusedStoredSessionId` listener, mirroring the existing [`$selectedStoredSessionId.listen(...)`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/41a07f5b8451f88a8b8b5adfc0cfdc2ada0a1f90/apps/desktop/src/store/session-states.ts#L737-L745) just below it. Calling the helper from the tile branch of `focusOpenSession` alone is not enough, that path is only reached from the sidebar, ⌘K, and notification jumps, whereas clicking a tile tab goes through [`activateTreePane`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/41a07f5b8451f88a8b8b5adfc0cfdc2ada0a1f90/apps/desktop/src/components/pane-shell/tree/renderer/tree-group.tsx#L470) and never reaches it. `setSelectedStoredSessionId` can then delegate to the same helper, keeping one clear path.

Keeping this independent of `$selectedStoredSessionId` is the point: a tile can be the visible, focused conversation without ever being the main selection.

## Related

Related to but not a duplicate of https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/70449. That one is about opening a session wrongly clearing a *working* state. This is the inverse: focusing a completed session fails to clear its *unread* state.

## Environment

- Hermes Desktop on macOS
- Hermes Agent v0.19.0
- Code references are against `main` as of 2026-07-29

items.body:
## Bug Description

The Hermes Desktop app launches a separate backend process (`hermes serve`) for **every** profile found in `~/.hermes/profiles/`, plus the default profile, on every startup. This causes:

1. **Timeout loading skills** — The desktop tries to query all backends simultaneously, hitting the 15s timeout (`Error invoking remote method 'hermes:api': Error: Timed out connecting to Hermes backend after 15000ms`)
2. **Excessive memory usage** — 3+ Python processes running when only 1 is needed
3. **Slow startup** — Each backend must fully boot before the desktop is usable

## Expected Behavior

The desktop should only launch the backend for the **active/selected profile**, not all profiles. Alternatively, there should be a `--profile` flag on `hermes desktop` to control which profile's backend to start.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Have multiple profiles in `~/.hermes/profiles/` (e.g., `nt8-developer`, `negocio-br`)
2. Launch `hermes desktop`
3. Observe 3 backend processes running simultaneously
4. Skills panel shows `Skills failed to load` with timeout error

## Evidence from Logs (desktop.log)

```
[hermes] Starting Hermes backend via Hermes at C:\Users\amarober\AppData\Local\hermes\hermes-agent
[hermes] HERMES_BACKEND_READY port=50711
[hermes] Starting Hermes backend for profile "nt8-developer" via Hermes at ...
[hermes] HERMES_BACKEND_READY port=54572
[hermes] Starting Hermes backend for profile "negocio-br" via Hermes at ...
[hermes] HERMES_BACKEND_READY port=55085
```

## Environment

- OS: Windows 10
- Hermes version: latest (desktop-build-stamp: 2026-07-29T14:42:37)
- Profiles: default + 2 additional profiles
- Skills: 100 skills (54MB total)

## Suggested Fix

Either:
- Only launch the backend for the currently active profile
- Add a `--profile` flag to `hermes desktop` so users can choose which profile to load
- Lazy-load profile backends only when the user switches to them in the UI

items.title: CLI crash on startup when voice.record_key uses alt (e.g. alt+v): prompt_toolkit rejects 'a-v' key format

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

items.body:
## Problem

Setting `voice.record_key: alt+v` in `~/.hermes/config.yaml` causes Hermes CLI to crash at startup with:

```
Error: Invalid key: a-v
```

## Root Cause

1. `hermes_cli/voice.py::normalize_voice_record_key_for_prompt_toolkit("alt+v")` returns `"a-v"` (line 174)
2. `cli.py` passes it to `@kb.add(_voice_key)` at line 15371
3. prompt_toolkit 3.0.52 `_parse_key("a-v")` tries `Keys("a-v")` → `ValueError` (no `a-v` in Keys enum), then checks `len("a-v") != 1` → raises `ValueError("Invalid key: a-v")`
4. The `try/except` at `cli.py:15361` wraps config loading only, not the `@kb.add()` call, so the exception propagates and crashes the CLI

prompt_toolkit 3.0.52 has no Alt/Meta modifier keys in its `Keys` enum — only `c-*` (Ctrl) prefix entries exist. `a-*` format is unsupported.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. `echo 'voice:\n  record_key: alt+v' >> ~/.hermes/config.yaml`
2. Run `hermes`
3. Observe `Error: Invalid key: a-v`

## Expected

Alt+V should work as a voice record key. In prompt_toolkit, Alt+key should be bound as a two-key sequence `(Keys.Escape, "<key>")`.

## Suggested Fix

Two issues to fix:

### 1. `cli.py` — `@kb.add()` should be in the try/except or validate before binding

The `@kb.add(_voice_key)` at line 15371 is outside the `try` block. Any invalid key crashes the CLI. The binding call should either:
- Be inside the `try/except`
- Or validate the key string before passing to `kb.add()`

### 2. `hermes_cli/voice.py::normalize_voice_record_key_for_prompt_toolkit` — Alt keys need special handling

The function currently returns `"a-v"` for alt keys, but this format is incompatible with prompt_toolkit. For Alt modifiers, it should signal the caller to use `(Keys.Escape, "<key>")` instead of a single `"a-<key>"` string.

### Workaround

Set `voice.record_key: ctrl+b` (the default) — Ctrl keys work fine.

## Environment

- Hermes version: latest (commit `41a07f5`)
- prompt_toolkit: 3.0.52
- OS: Linux

items.body:
# Desktop API Keys tab has no way to remove provider API keys

## What I observed
In Hermes Desktop, the Settings > API Keys tab shows discovered provider key
variables, but there is no remove/delete control for them. When all keys are
removed from the environment, the tab shows only a `NoProviderKeys` empty
state with no way to manage keys from the GUI.

## What I verified in source

### Desktop API Keys UI
`apps/desktop/src/app/settings/keys-settings.tsx` renders `<CredentialKeyCard>`
and reads key metadata from `apps/desktop/src/app/settings/credential-key-ui.tsx`
via `isKeyVar()` and `ProviderKeyRows`. The credential rows display the key
name/value but expose **no delete button or remove action**.

### Desktop provider keys tab state
`apps/desktop/src/i18n/en.ts:842-850` includes `removeConfirm`,
`removeKeyManaged`, `removeExternalGeneric`, `removeTerminalConfirm`, and
`removedMessage` strings, but those are only wired up in
`apps/desktop/src/app/settings/providers-settings.tsx:258-423` for the
Providers page, not in `keys-settings.tsx`. The Providers page uses these
strings for `handleDisconnect`/`handleTerminalDisconnect`, so the key-removal
copy is orphaned from the actual API-keys tab.

## Root cause
The desktop API-keys panel reads credential state but never renders a removal
control. The only place `deleteEnvVar` is called from Settings is:
- `apps/desktop/src/app/settings/env-credentials.tsx:148`
- `apps/desktop/src/app/settings/toolset-config-panel.tsx:127`

Neither path is reached from `keys-settings.tsx`. As a result, unused provider
API keys can only be removed from an external shell or by editing the profile
`.env` manually.

## Repro steps
1. Open Hermes Desktop Settings > API Keys.
2. Observe provider keys listed with no remove/delete affordance.
3. Switch to Settings > Providers and note that removal copy exists there,
   but that route either directs to an external CLI (external providers) or
   performs OAuth disconnect, not generic key deletion.
4. There is no desktop GUI path to remove a simple `OPENAI_API_KEY` style
   env var from the API Keys tab.

## Suggested fix
Add a remove action to `ProviderKeyRows` / `CredentialKeyCard` in
`credential-key-ui.tsx` and wire it through `keys-settings.tsx` to call
`deleteEnvVar(key)` + `refreshEnvVars()`, mirroring the existing
`env-credentials.tsx` pattern.

items.body:
# Bug: Removing auth providers in Desktop does not clear credentials and UI reverts

## What I observed
When removing an auth-based provider from Hermes Desktop (Settings > Providers
> Remove), the provider entry reappears after a refresh and the associated API
key/env credential remains set in the profile environment. The removal appears
to succeed briefly, then reverts.

## What I verified in source

### Desktop removal path
`apps/desktop/src/app/settings/providers-settings.tsx:407-425` calls
`disconnectOAuthProvider(provider.id)` and on success refreshes the OAuth list.

`apps/desktop/src/hermes.ts:853-859` defines `disconnectOAuthProvider` as a
`DELETE /api/providers/oauth/{providerId}` request through
`window.hermesDesktop.api`.

### Gateway/backend
There is **no** `DELETE /api/providers/oauth/{id}` handler in
`gateway/platforms/api_server.py`. The only `/api/providers/oauth/*` routes
registered there are:
- `GET /api/providers/oauth`
- `POST /api/providers/oauth/{id}/start`
- `POST /api/providers/oauth/{id}/submit`
- `GET /api/providers/oauth/sessions/{sessionId}`

(`gateway/platforms/api_server.py:1808-1822`)

That means the Desktop `DELETE` call has no matching backend route and returns
`404`/method-not-allowed. The frontend catches the error in
`handleDisconnect` (`providers-settings.tsx:406-425`), but because
`disconnectOAuthProvider` is awaited inside a try/catch that shows a toast and
continues, the failed removal still triggers `refreshOAuthProviders()`, which
re-reads the provider list from env/config and repopulates the row — making it
_appear_ to revert.

### Env/credential side
Even if the OAuth session were cleared, the env-var credential itself is not
removed. The only Desktop-side env deletion paths are:
- `apps/desktop/src/app/settings/env-credentials.tsx:148` (`deleteEnvVar(key)`)
- `apps/desktop/src/app/settings/toolset-config-panel.tsx:127`

Neither is invoked from `providers-settings.tsx`'s `handleDisconnect`. So the
provider row stays visible because the key is still present, and subsequent
runtime/provider resolution re-creates the auth surface.

## Root cause
1. Desktop sends `DELETE /api/providers/oauth/{id}`, but the backend has no
   such route.
2. The Desktop disconnect handler does not clear the provider's API key from
   the profile `.env` or `config.yaml` after disconnect, so the provider
   reappears on the next refresh.

## Repro steps
1. Connect an auth-based provider in Hermes Desktop (e.g., a provider with
   `oauth` flow).
2. Open Settings > Providers and click Remove (trash icon).
3. Observe: success toast appears, but after a few seconds the provider card
   reappears.
4. Inspect `~/.hermes/.env` / profile `.env`: the provider's key env var is
   still set.

## Suggested fix
1. Add a `DELETE /api/providers/oauth/{provider_id}` route in
   `gateway/platforms/api_server.py` that removes the OAuth credential and
   clears any stored session/state for that provider.
2. In Desktop `handleDisconnect`, after `disconnectOAuthProvider` succeeds,
   also remove the provider's env credential via `deleteEnvVar` /
   `remove_provider_env_credential` so the row cannot reappear from config.

items.title: fix: faster-whisper VAD filter + default thresholds drop non-English speech

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

items.body:
## Problem

Local STT (faster-whisper) returns empty transcription for non-English speech (Chinese in this case), even though:
- Microphone captures audio correctly (WAV files are reasonable size, amplitude > 2000)
- Language detection succeeds (`lang=zh, prob=1.000`)
- No errors in logs — just `Transcribed ... (base, lang=zh, 5.0s audio)` with transcript `""`

## Root Cause

Two silent failures stacked:

### 1. Silero VAD filter removes all audio (primary cause)
The faster-whisper VAD filter (enabled by default in `build_local_transcribe_kwargs`) falsely flags Chinese speech as non-speech and removes the ENTIRE recording. Log tell:
```
INFO:faster_whisper:VAD filter removed 00:05.000 of audio
DEBUG:faster_whisper:VAD filter kept the following audio segments: 
```
The VAD filter runs inside faster-whisper **before** the transcription model, so the model never sees any audio → 0 segments.

### 2. Default confidence thresholds too aggressive for non-English
Even without VAD, faster-whispers internal `no_speech_threshold=0.6` / `log_prob_threshold=-1.0` silently drop low-confidence segments. Non-English speech tends to have lower `avg_logprob`, so these defaults filter out segments before they return to the caller.

Additionally, `build_local_transcribe_kwargs()` reads `stt.local.no_speech_prob_threshold` and `stt.local.logprob_threshold` from config but only uses them in Hermes own post-filter (`_join_confident_segments` → `_is_hallucinated_segment`). It does **not** pass them to `model.transcribe()`, so faster-whispers internal defaults always apply — making the config options effectively dead for the first gate.

## Fix

### Code change: `tools/transcription_tools.py`

In `build_local_transcribe_kwargs()`, pass `no_speech_threshold` and `log_prob_threshold` through to `model.transcribe()` kwargs, mapped from the existing config keys `stt.local.no_speech_prob_threshold` / `stt.local.logprob_threshold` with the same defaults (0.6, -1.0):

```python
for fw_key, cfg_key, default in (
    ("no_speech_threshold", "no_speech_prob_threshold", _NO_SPEECH_PROB_THRESHOLD_DEFAULT),
    ("log_prob_threshold",  "logprob_threshold",        _LOGPROB_THRESHOLD_DEFAULT),
):
    try:
        val = float(local_cfg.get(cfg_key, default))
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        val = default
    kwargs[fw_key] = val
```

This ensures faster-whispers internal filtering uses the same thresholds Hermes `_is_hallucinated_segment` post-filter uses, so segments arent double-killed.

### Config workaround (for users until the fix ships)

```bash
# Disable VAD (Silero VAD too aggressive for some microphones/voices)
hermes config set stt.local.vad false

# Relax confidence thresholds (defaults 0.6/-1.0 designed for English)
hermes config set stt.local.no_speech_prob_threshold 0.9
hermes config set stt.local.logprob_threshold -2.0

# Set language for non-English speech
hermes config set stt.language zh
```

## Files changed

- `tools/transcription_tools.py` — `build_local_transcribe_kwargs()`: pass threshold kwargs to `model.transcribe()`
- `tests/tools/test_stt_silence_hallucinations.py` — added `test_thresholds_configurable_in_transcribe()` + assertions in `test_hardened_kwargs_reach_model()`

## Verification

All 172 tests pass:
```
tests/tools/test_stt_silence_hallucinations.py ...............  19 passed
tests/tools/test_transcription_tools.py ...................... 153 passed
```

End-to-end test with recorded Chinese speech:
```
Recording 5s... Speak Chinese!
Max amp: 3020
success: True
transcript: "我认识了 我认识了"
```

Before fix: same recording returned `transcript: ""` with no errors.

items.title: Auto-resolve X/Twitter URLs shared in chat instead of asking user for context
items.body:
## Feature Request

### Problem
When a user shares an X/Twitter URL in a messaging platform (Slack, Telegram, Discord), the gateway includes the URL in the message but does not auto-fetch the post content. The agent has to either:
1. Use the browser tool to navigate to the URL (slow, resource-heavy, may hit bot detection)
2. Ask the user to provide context (bad UX — the user shared the link specifically so the agent could read it)

This was observed in a Slack thread where a user shared an X post link. The Slack gateway included a link preview attachment with the URL, but the agent asked the user for context instead of fetching the post content directly.

### Proposed Solution
When a message contains an X/Twitter URL (x.com/*/status/* or twitter.com/*/status/*), the agent should automatically fetch and read the post content before responding. Options:

1. **Gateway-level URL expansion**: The gateway could auto-fetch X post content when a URL is detected and include it inline in the message context (similar to how Slack link unfurls work, but with actual post text).

2. **Agent-level URL auto-resolution**: The system prompt or agent loop could include a convention that when an X URL is present, the agent should immediately use available tools (xurl if installed, or browser_navigate) to read the post content rather than asking the user.

3. **xurl integration**: If `xurl` is installed and authenticated, use `xurl read <URL>` as a fast, lightweight fetch that does not require a full browser session. This avoids bot detection issues and is much faster than browser navigation.

### Context
- `xurl` skill exists but `xurl` CLI may not be installed on all systems
- Browser tool works but is heavyweight for a simple text fetch
- The agent should never ask the user for context that it can fetch itself from a URL they explicitly shared

### Environment
- Platform: Slack gateway
- Observed with: x.com/grok/status/2082495043177255005
- Agent asked user for context instead of reading the post directly

items.title: Desktop: Could not connect to Hermes gateway on Chinese Windows (GBK) — hermes serve headless token extraction fails

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

labels.name: sweeper:risk-platform-windows
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break or behave differently on native Windows

items.body:
## Symptom

After updating Hermes, the desktop GUI shows "Could not connect to Hermes gateway" on every launch. The app enters a restart loop: it spawns `hermes serve`, the backend starts successfully (visible in logs), but the renderer fails to connect to the WebSocket gateway.

**Key observation: the terminal CLI works fine** — only the desktop GUI is affected.

## Environment

- **OS**: Windows 10 (Chinese locale, GBK system encoding)
- **Hermes**: v0.19.0 (b6729ba)
- **Desktop app**: Electron (win-unpacked)
- **Connection mode**: local (spawns `hermes serve`)

## Workarounds

1. Set Windows display language to English (non-GBK locale) → works
2. Open Gateway Settings → re-apply "local" connection mode → works (triggers a clean restart)

## What the logs show

**1. Initial boot (pre-update, old `dashboard` mode) — GBK crash:**
`HERMES_DASHBOARD_READY` → `UnicodeDecodeError: gbk codec can't decode byte 0x94` → backend crashes

**2. After update (headless `serve` mode):**
`HERMES_BACKEND_READY port=xxx` → `[boot] could not read served dashboard token (Hermes backend): 404: {"error":"Headless backend (hermes serve): web UI disabled — use \`hermes dashboard\` for the browser UI."}` → `[boot] Hermes backend is ready. Finalizing desktop startup` → renderer shows error

**3. Renderer ECONNRESET:**
`[renderer console] Error invoking remote method 'hermes:api': Error: read ECONNRESET`

**4. Restart loop:**
`[bootstrap] reset requested by renderer` → `Ignoring stale Hermes backend exit (1)` → spawn again

## Analysis (AI-generated, may not be accurate)

The desktop app (main process) calls `adoptServedDashboardToken()` in `dashboard-token.ts` which fetches `GET /` from the backend to extract the session token from the SPA HTML. However, `hermes serve` is a headless backend — it sets `HERMES_SERVE_HEADLESS=1`, which disables the SPA mount. The `mount_spa()` function in `web_server.py` returns early, registering a catch-all route that returns 404 with "Headless backend (hermes serve): web UI disabled".

The `adoptServedDashboardToken` function catches the 404 error and returns the fallback token (spawn token), so the main process probe succeeds. But the renderer's subsequent WebSocket connection attempt fails with ECONNRESET, triggering a restart loop.

The root cause may be related to:
1. **GBK encoding**: The initial crash on Chinese Windows (GBK) triggered the update, and the post-update `serve` mode has a different code path that doesn't handle the GBK locale correctly
2. **Token extraction**: `adoptServedDashboardToken` should skip the HTML extraction when the backend is running in headless `serve` mode, since the token is already passed via `HERMES_DASHBOARD_SESSION_TOKEN` environment variable
3. **Renderer connection**: The renderer's WebSocket connection fails while the main process probe succeeds — the reason for this discrepancy is unclear

## Attached files

- Full desktop.log (7242 lines) — saved to Hermeswork
- Error screenshot (showing "Hermes couldn't start" dialog)

items.body: ### Bug Description I checked the suggested duplicate issues (#70619, #58387 and #51215), but this appears to be a different problem. The installation is healthy, the backend exits correctly, the Python processes can be terminated successfully, and the issue persists even after a full Windows reboot. This appears to be a false process detection or updater state synchronization issue in the Desktop updater. ## Summary Hermes Desktop (Windows) is unable to install updates through the built-in updater. The updater always aborts with: > Update didn't finish > Update aborted: another Hermes process is using this installation. The update worked normally several times on the same day. After one successful update, every subsequent update started failing with this error. The problem persists even after a full Windows restart. The desktop application itself continues to work normally. Only the updater fails. ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Install Hermes Desktop on Windows. 2. Update successfully several times using the built-in updater. 3. A newer update becomes available. 4. Click "Update". 5. Hermes shows "Backend stopped". 6. Updater aborts with: "Another Hermes process is using this installation." 7. Restart Windows completely. 8. Try updating again. Result: The exact same error appears every time. ### Expected Behavior The updater should stop the Hermes backend, replace the application files, and complete the update successfully. ### Actual Behavior The updater reports that Hermes processes are still using the installation even after: - Backend reports "Backend stopped" - Windows has been restarted - Hermes processes have been manually terminated The update never completes. ### Affected Component Setup / Installation ### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related) _No response_ ### Debug Report ```shell I investigated the running processes manually. Initially two Python processes existed: Process 1 Executable: C:\Users\\AppData\Local\hermes\hermes-agent\venv\Scripts\python.exe Command: python.exe -m hermes_cli.main gateway run Process 2 Executable: C:\Users\\AppData\Roaming\uv\python\cpython-3.11-windows-x86_64-none\python.exe Command: python.exe -m hermes_cli.main gateway run I terminated the Hermes venv process manually: taskkill /F /PID Result: SUCCESS: The process has been terminated. Running: tasklist | findstr python afterwards returned no Hermes Python process. Despite this, the updater still reports that another Hermes process is using the installation and refuses to continue. This also happens after a complete Windows reboot. ``` ### Operating System Windows 11 ### Python Version Bundled Python (Hermes Desktop) Additional runtime detected: Python 3.11 (uv managed) ### Hermes Version 0.19.0 ### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional) ```shell Popup: Update didn't finish Update aborted: another Hermes process is using this installation. These processes must be stopped before updating. Backend notification: Backend stopped Hermes background process exited. ``` ### Root Cause Analysis (optional) This appears to be a Windows Desktop updater issue rather than an actual running-process issue. Reasons: - Updates succeeded multiple times before this started happening. - Restarting Windows does not resolve it. - The updater reports "Backend stopped". - Hermes processes can be manually terminated successfully. - Even after termination, the updater still believes Hermes is running. It looks like the updater is incorrectly detecting running processes or failing to recognize that the backend has already exited. ### Proposed Fix (optional) Possible areas to investigate: - Windows process detection logic used by the updater. - Backend shutdown synchronization before update begins. - False positives when checking gateway/background Python processes. - File locking detection after backend exit. - Verify that the updater refreshes process state after shutdown instead of using stale detection results. ### Are you willing to submit a PR for this? - [ ] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

items.title: pyproject.toml py-modules omits four hermes_state_* modules — session store silently disabled in every wheel-based install (found on NixOS)

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

items.body:
## Summary

`hermes_state.py` imports four sibling top-level modules that are not listed in `[tool.setuptools] py-modules`, so they are never packaged. Any install built from this `pyproject.toml` (pip/uv wheel, nix, distro packaging) starts with the SQLite session store disabled: no persistence, no `--continue` / `--resume`, no session search. Git installs are unaffected, because they run from the repo tree where the files are present — which is likely why this hasn't surfaced.

Failure is soft. Hermes prints a warning and keeps going, so unless you read it you just quietly stop having session history.

```
⚠ Session store unavailable — this conversation will NOT be saved to disk and
  cannot be resumed later. Searching past sessions is also disabled.
  Reason: No module named 'hermes_state_common'
  Fix the state.db store (e.g. `hermes update` to rebuild the venv) to restore persistence.
```

The suggested fix in that message (`hermes update` to rebuild the venv) cannot help — the modules are absent from the distribution itself, not from the venv.

## Cause

`hermes_state.py` (v0.19.0):

```python
46: from hermes_state_common import (  # noqa: F401  (re-exported for back-compat)
71: from hermes_state_portability import SessionPortabilityMixin
72: from hermes_state_schema import SessionSchemaMixin
73: from hermes_state_search import SessionSearchMixin
```

`pyproject.toml:348` lists `hermes_state` but none of its four dependencies:

```toml
py-modules = ["run_agent", "model_tools", "toolsets", "batch_runner", "trajectory_compressor",
              "toolset_distributions", "cli", "hermes_bootstrap", "hermes_constants",
              "hermes_state", "hermes_time", "hermes_logging", "utils", "mcp_serve"]
```

The build backend is `setuptools.build_meta`, so `py-modules` is what decides which top-level modules land in the wheel. The four also import each other, so all four are needed — adding only `hermes_state_common` moves the error along to `hermes_state_portability`.

## Reproduce

```bash
# any wheel-based install of 0.19.0, e.g.
python -m build && pip install dist/hermes_agent-0.19.0-*.whl
python -c "import hermes_state"
# ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'hermes_state_common'
```

Or diff the installed tree against the source tree — these are the top-level modules present in the repo but absent from `site-packages`:

```
hermes_state_common.py
hermes_state_portability.py
hermes_state_schema.py
hermes_state_search.py
```

## Suggested fix

```toml
py-modules = ["run_agent", "model_tools", "toolsets", "batch_runner", "trajectory_compressor",
              "toolset_distributions", "cli", "hermes_bootstrap", "hermes_constants",
              "hermes_state", "hermes_state_common", "hermes_state_portability",
              "hermes_state_schema", "hermes_state_search", "hermes_time",
              "hermes_logging", "utils", "mcp_serve"]
```

A guard would help too: an import-time smoke test over `py-modules` in CI would have caught this, since the list is hand-maintained and drifts whenever a module is split.

## Environment

- hermes-agent 0.19.0, flake rev `bc74700`
- Installed via `nix profile install github:NousResearch/hermes-agent` (NixOS). I know NixOS isn't officially supported — the packaging bug is not NixOS-specific, it affects any non-git install, which is why I'm reporting it rather than working around it locally.
- Workaround in use: the four modules copied to a directory on `PYTHONPATH`.

## Possibly unrelated

`mini_swe_runner.py` is also a top-level module in the repo but absent from `py-modules`. Nothing imports it, so this may well be deliberate — flagging only in case it isn't.

items.title: Copilot route: reasoning_effort 'ultra' clamps to 'medium', making the strongest setting weaker than 'high'

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

items.body:
## Summary

On the GitHub Copilot / GitHub Models route, `_github_models_reasoning_extra_body` clamps an unsupported reasoning effort to **`medium`**. Because `ultra` is not in Copilot's advertised effort list for any Claude model, selecting the *strongest* level in the Hermes picker silently produces **less thinking than selecting `high`**.

The effort selector is monotonic in the UI but non-monotonic in what's actually sent.

## Repro

Live Copilot catalog (`hermes_cli.models.fetch_github_model_catalog`) reports:

```
claude-opus-5     -> ['low','medium','high','xhigh','max']
claude-opus-4.8   -> ['low','medium','high','xhigh','max']
claude-opus-4.7   -> ['low','medium','high','xhigh','max']
claude-opus-4.6   -> ['low','medium','high','max']
claude-sonnet-5   -> ['low','medium','high','xhigh','max']
```

Hermes' global effort set (`hermes_constants.py:808`) is `minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh, max, ultra` — a superset. Driving the real method on `claude-opus-5`:

| requested | sent to API |
|---|---|
| minimal | low |
| low | low |
| medium | medium |
| high | high |
| xhigh | xhigh |
| max | max |
| **ultra** | **medium** ⬅ |

Rank sequence over the ladder, opus-5: `[0, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 1]` — the last step drops.
Same on opus-4.6: `[0, 0, 1, 2, 2, 3, 1]`.

## Cause

`run_agent.py` (~L6686, `AIAgent._github_models_reasoning_extra_body`):

```python
if requested_effort == "xhigh" and "xhigh" not in supported_efforts and "high" in supported_efforts:
    requested_effort = "high"
elif requested_effort not in supported_efforts:
    if requested_effort == "minimal" and "low" in supported_efforts:
        requested_effort = "low"
    elif "medium" in supported_efforts:
        requested_effort = "medium"      # <-- ultra lands here
    else:
        requested_effort = supported_efforts[0]
```

`xhigh` and `minimal` each get a hand-written special case; `ultra` (and `max`, on any future model lacking it) has none and falls to the `medium` default.

This is route-specific. The direct-Anthropic path is correct — `agent/anthropic_adapter.py:ADAPTIVE_EFFORT_MAP` maps `ultra -> max`. `agent/transports/codex.py:230` and `agent/lmstudio_reasoning.py:32` also clamp `ultra` to their respective ceilings. Only the Copilot/GitHub-Models path inverts.

## Proposed fix

Replace the per-level special cases with an ordered ladder and clamp toward the nearest supported level **in the same direction** — an over-ceiling request walks down, an under-floor request walks up. Generalizes `xhigh`/`minimal` handling instead of enumerating it, so a future level added to `REASONING_EFFORT_LEVELS` can't reintroduce the inversion.

```python
_EFFORT_LADDER = ["minimal", "low", "medium", "high", "xhigh", "max", "ultra"]

if requested_effort not in supported_efforts:
    if requested_effort in _EFFORT_LADDER:
        idx = _EFFORT_LADDER.index(requested_effort)
        downgrade = next(
            (lvl for lvl in reversed(_EFFORT_LADDER[:idx]) if lvl in supported_efforts),
            None,
        )
        upgrade = next(
            (lvl for lvl in _EFFORT_LADDER[idx + 1:] if lvl in supported_efforts),
            None,
        )
        requested_effort = downgrade or upgrade or supported_efforts[0]
    elif "medium" in supported_efforts:
        requested_effort = "medium"
    else:
        requested_effort = supported_efforts[0]
```

Preserves every currently-correct mapping (`xhigh -> high` on 4.6, `minimal -> low`) and fixes `ultra -> max`.

## Verification

Behavioral test driving the real method with a stubbed `github_model_reasoning_efforts`, asserting the **invariant** (a stronger request never yields a weaker effort) rather than freezing the catalog:

```
                        pre-fix   post-fix
opus-5   ultra   ->     medium    max
opus-4.6 ultra   ->     medium    max
opus-5   xhigh   ->     xhigh     xhigh     (unchanged)
opus-4.6 xhigh   ->     high      high      (unchanged)
opus-5   minimal ->     low       low       (unchanged)

monotonicity opus-5:   [0,0,1,2,3,4,1] FAIL  ->  [0,0,1,2,3,4,4] PASS
monotonicity opus-4.6: [0,0,1,2,2,3,1] FAIL  ->  [0,0,1,2,2,3,3] PASS
```

Fails against pre-fix code, passes against the fix. Happy to open a PR with the patch + test if useful.

## Environment

hermes-agent 0.19.0, macOS 26.5.2, provider `github-copilot`, model `claude-opus-5`.

items.title: auth: Codex OAuth cancel doesn't stop device-code worker; can still write token to wrong profile

labels.name: duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: sweeper:risk-security-boundary
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may affect sandboxing, auth, credentials, or sensitive data

labels.name: sweeper:risk-compatibility
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break existing users, config, migrations, defaults, or upgrades

items.body:
## Summary
Cancelling an OpenAI Codex device-code OAuth flow does not stop the background polling worker, and if the user authorizes anyway after cancelling, credentials are still written — potentially to the wrong profile.

## Root cause
- The poll loop (`hermes_cli/web_server.py`, around the `while time.monotonic() < deadline: ...` block near line 11296) never re-checks whether the session was cancelled.
- The target profile is resolved lazily via `_oauth_session_profile(session_id)` only at write time (~line 11347), not captured up front.
- `DELETE /api/providers/oauth/sessions/{session_id}` (~line 11444) only does `_oauth_sessions.pop(session_id, None)` — no cancellation token/event, and it does not signal the worker thread.
- After the pop, `_oauth_session_profile(session_id)` returns `None` (session no longer in the dict), which falls through to whatever profile is "current" at completion time, not the profile that was originally selected when the flow started.

## Impact
- User believes the auth flow was aborted, but credentials may still be written later.
- Credentials can land in the wrong (current/default) profile instead of the originally targeted one, breaking profile isolation.
- The worker keeps consuming a thread/polling the provider until session expiry even after cancel.

## Suggested fix (root cause)
- Track cancellation via a per-session event/flag, checked before every poll iteration, before the code exchange, and before the token write.
- Capture the validated target profile once at session start (immutable for the life of the worker) instead of re-resolving it at write time.
- Require the session to still exist, be uncancelled, and match the same provider/profile before persisting tokens.

## Reproduction
Local deterministic repro built with `TestClient`, fake HTTP responses, and sentinel tokens: worker paused right after publishing the device code, `DELETE` called, poll then approved. Result: cancel endpoint returns 200, session removed, but the worker still finishes and calls the token-save path once, with the profile scope resolved to `None` instead of the original profile.

items.title: codex: retry after response.completed duplicates an already-finished, billed inference

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: area/usage-cost
labels.description: Token accounting, usage reporting, billing, cost tracking

items.body:
## Summary
When a Codex Responses stream delivers output, `usage`, and `response.completed`, but the socket then fails during the post-terminal drain (used to finalize the Relay transport), Hermes treats the failure as transient and starts a brand-new inference — even though the first one already completed and was billed.

## Root cause
- `agent/codex_runtime.py` correctly assembles the terminal response from `response.completed` (~lines 1350-1368).
- Immediately after, the code drains the event iterator again just to consume the transport's end marker / finalize Relay (~lines 1369-1374).
- A single `except (RemoteProtocolError, ReadTimeout, ConnectError, ConnectionError)` wraps **both** the assembly step and this post-terminal drain (~lines 1375-1384). On error there, it `continue`s into the generic retry path, discarding the already-built terminal response and opening a whole new request — with no special-casing for "we already received a valid `response.completed`".

## Impact
- Duplicates inference and cost on any transport error that happens strictly after the terminal event.
- Can duplicate semantic output and add latency.
- Undercounts total cost, since the discarded-but-completed attempt's usage is never reported to accounting (only the second attempt's `usage` reaches billing).

## Suggested fix (root cause)
Once a valid terminal event (`response.completed`) has been observed and assembled, a drain/cleanup error must not trigger a new inference. Return the already-assembled terminal response and record the drain failure only as a transport/Relay finalization warning, separate from the pre-terminal retry path.

## Reproduction
Deterministic fake stream: first stream emits `response.output_item.done` → `response.completed` (120 tokens) → `RemoteProtocolError` during close. Second (retried) stream returns a normal `OK` response. Result: 2 physical calls made; only the second response's usage (`120` was actually usage on the first, second stream had its own) reaches accounting; the first, already-complete response is silently discarded.

items.title: auth: fallback config resolves API key via raw os.getenv(), bypassing secret_scope profile isolation

labels.name: comp/agent

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: sweeper:risk-security-boundary
